explanation: 该论文主要关注自然气候解决方案与植物入侵之间的相互作用，尽管涉及碳汇和土地利用管理，但并未直接涉及大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测或大气成分分析等。
authors: Evelyn M Beaury;Jonathan M Levine
title: Feedbacks between natural climate solutions and plant invasions
abstract: Biological invasions and carbon sequestration guide many modern-day land management decisions. However, intersections between invasions and natural climate solutions (NCS)—actions to maintain or increase the land carbon sink—have not received adequate attention in either the invasion or climate mitigation literature. We therefore review how plant invasions affect NCS and vice versa, focusing on reductions in emissions and carbon removals associated with avoided habitat conversion, restoration, forest and cropland management, agroforestry, and optimal grazing. We find that plant invasions can interfere with rapid NCS implementation and reduce the durability of carbon storage in many systems, although there are cases in which invasive plants increase carbon storage, creating biodiversity-climate mitigation trade-offs. At the same time, studies find that several NCS increase community resistance/resilience to invasions, and do so in forests, in particular, which can suppress invasive species spread in these systems. These dynamics suggest a positive feedback loop between NCS and invasions, in which NCS facilitate invasion control, and successful invasion control, in turn, eases further NCS implementation. This feedback could accelerate gains in land-based carbon storage and generate co-benefits for biodiversity, provided that NCS projects receive resources for sustained invasive species management. We highlight areas in need of further research, including how financial mechanisms for climate action could be used to overcome invasion-induced implementation barriers.

explanation: 该论文研究全球平均温度的变化趋势，探讨了温度加速的现象，这与大气环境遥感技术中的温度监测和分析密切相关。虽然论文没有直接提及卫星观测或空气质量监测，但其对温度变化趋势的分析方法和技术对大气环境遥感领域有重要参考价值。
authors: J Eduardo Vera-Valdés
title: Detecting acceleration in global mean temperature using supralinear trends
abstract: Whether global mean surface temperature has accelerated has received opposite answers in quick succession, reported as undetectable on data to 2023 and as significant on data to 2024. This raises two questions: since when is acceleration detectable, and how far does the answer depend on the test used? We show that structural-break tests, often used for this purpose, cannot reliably date the onset of a continuously accelerating warming rate. We therefore test for curvature directly, under specifications whose null is exactly a constant warming rate and whose alternative is curvature rather than a break. One is a linearithmic trend, which grows faster than linear but more slowly than any polynomial of degree greater than one; the other estimates the curvature freely from the data. We report alongside them the quadratic trend used in the recent literature. Over 1970–2025, in a single full-sample test, the linearithmic and quadratic coefficients are positive and statistically significant in all five major temperature datasets once El Niño and solar variability are controlled for. The onset of acceleration is dated by re-estimating over expanding windows and correcting for multiple testing. Under the linearithmic specification, acceleration first becomes detectable in windows ending in mid-2023 for NOAA, late 2023 for GISTEMP and mid-2024 for ERA5, and not yet in HadCRUT or Berkeley. The free-curvature specification agrees on direction but rejects in fewer datasets, since estimating the shape costs precision. The linearithmic specification implies the least curvature of the three, with an acceleration that declines over time, and so the lowest warming of the three when extended to 2050.

explanation: 该论文的主题是关于北欧森林的碳封存和氮预算的协调，主要涉及生态学和森林管理领域，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）没有直接关系。
authors: Filip Moldan;Sara Jutterström;Johanna Stadmark;Anu Akujärvi;Martin Forsius;Kari Austnes;Heleen A de Wit;Jesper Bak
title: Reconciling carbon sequestration with nitrogen budgets in Nordic forests

explanation: 该论文研究的是南大洋印度扇区的氧气化趋势及其驱动因素，涉及卫星和再分析数据，这与大气环境遥感技术（如卫星观测、大气成分分析）密切相关。
authors: N N S Vishnu;P Sabu;A R Anantha Krishnan;Soumyadeep Dutta;Sidhesh G Borker;E Sreevidya;Rahul Mohan
title: Trends and drivers of recent oxygenation in the Indian sector of the Southern Ocean
abstract: Integrating in-situ observations from austral summers 2011 and 2025 with satellite and reanalysis data (1993–2025) reveals significant oxygenation across the Indian sector of the Southern Ocean (ISSO), with the strongest trends in the Polar (PZ) and Antarctic Zones (AZ). Observations along 57.5° E show elevated dissolved oxygen (DO), poleward retreat of the winter water (WW) layer, and partial shoaling of the oxygen minimum layer in 2025 relative to 2011. Combined effect of warming and salinification weakens stratification and promote circumpolar deep water (CDW) shoaling, driving enhanced ventilation and oxygenation. Declining apparent oxygen utilization is consistent with enhanced ventilation, not solubility changes, as the dominant mechanism. Oxygenation spans from Antarctic surface water and WW through subantarctic mode water, Antarctic intermediate water, and CDW to Antarctic bottom water, indicating basin-wide ventilation reorganization. These findings contrast with widespread global ocean deoxygenation and highlight the importance of Southern Ocean ventilation for the global ocean oxygen inventory.

explanation: 该论文研究南极涡旋中下层平流层臭氧的测量和建模趋势，涉及卫星观测（如Aura Microwave Limb Sounder, MLS）和化学气候模型（WACCM），直接与大气环境遥感技术和大气成分分析相关。
authors: Lucien Froidevaux;Michael J. Schwartz;Douglas E. Kinnison;Nathaniel J. Livesey;Gloria L. Manney;Michelle L. Santee;William G. Read;Ryan A. Fuller
title: Trends in measured and modeled lower stratospheric Antarctic vortex ozone over the past two decades
abstract:
We examine 20 years (2004–2023) of vertical profiles of winter/spring lower stratospheric ozone inside the Antarctic vortex, based on satellite observations and a chemistry climate model. The observations show increases in the smallest ozone values, as well as trends consistent with a slow recovery from the long-term impact of ozone-depleting substances. The model also shows some reductions in lower stratospheric seasonal Antarctic ozone losses, in broad agreement with the observations. 
 We analyze 2004 to 2023 winter/spring lower stratospheric Antarctic ozone data from the Aura Microwave Limb Sounder (MLS), along with similarly sampled profiles from two simulations from the Whole Atmosphere Community Climate Model (WACCM) run with specified dynamics. One of these simulations uses fixed surface organic halogens from 1998 onward. The interannual variability in MLS vortex-average ozone is well matched by WACCM, although WACCM shows a slightly smaller seasonal decrease. Probability density functions of vortex ozone profiles reveal slow increases in the smallest values; WACCM shows good agreement with MLS distribution shifts and simple linear trends. We also use multivariate linear regression with two periodic functions and a proxy for polar stratospheric clouds to derive trends in vortex-average ozone during September and October. Calculated trends are consistent with slow Antarctic vortex ozone recovery from the impact of ozone-depleting substances, with values between ∼ 5 and 16 ppbv yr−1 in the 56–100 hPa layer. WACCM results agree well with those from MLS. The simulation with fixed surface organic halogens is consistent with zero trend. We also apply the Match technique, which follows MLS-observed parcels along trajectories to estimate vortex-average chemical ozone loss. Match estimates also show slow reductions in seasonal Antarctic ozone loss, although few of the Match results represent greater than two-sigma departures from zero. Our work confirms the emergence of ozone recovery, a key goal of the Aura mission, and underscores the importance of the 1987 Montreal Protocol and its Amendments in curtailing emissions of ozone-depleting substances.

explanation: 该论文研究了中国东部地区的有机气溶胶吸湿性，重点关注了生物质燃烧源的影响，这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测和气溶胶质构分析密切相关。
authors: Yunfei Wu;Jiwei Li;Zhisheng Zhang;Jun Tao;Yunjie Xia;Liang Ran;Zhaoze Deng
title: Source-dependent organic aerosol hygroscopicity in eastern China: observational evidence for conditional enhancement under biomass-burning influence
abstract:
Atmospheric particles affect climate by absorbing water and forming clouds, but how organic aerosols uptake water remains unclear. Our field measurements in rural eastern China show their hygroscopicity depends more on emission sources – especially biomass burning – than oxidation. Aging increases water uptake from biomass burning, but not from other sources. These results urge models to include source information for better climate predictions. 
 Aerosol hygroscopicity is a key property governing aerosol water uptake and aerosol–cloud interactions, yet the hygroscopicity of organic aerosol (OA) remains poorly constrained because of its chemical complexity and diverse emission sources. Here, OA hygroscopicity (κOA) was retrieved from comprehensive field observations at a rural site in eastern China using humidified light-scattering measurements and ZSR-based closure analysis. κOA exhibited pronounced temporal variability during winter, ranging from nearly zero to 0.49 with a mean value of 0.11 ± 0.11. Although OA was generally highly oxidized, κOA was only weakly correlated with the O:C ratio, indicating that bulk oxidation state alone cannot explain its variability. Instead, κOA increased systematically with biomass-burning influence. Atmospheric aging substantially enhanced κOA under biomass-burning-dominated conditions, whereas highly oxidized OA under weak biomass-burning influence remained weakly hygroscopic. These findings demonstrate that the hygroscopic response of OA to atmospheric aging is fundamentally source dependent and indicate that source-dependent parameterizations provide a more physically realistic framework than conventional oxidation-based approaches for representing OA hygroscopicity in atmospheric models.

explanation: 这篇论文研究的是傅里叶变换红外发射光谱法（FTIR emission spectroscopy）在测量大气热辐射时的功率校准问题，这与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，例如空气质量和大气成分分析。文中提到的NYAEM-FTS spectrometer和AERI等设备都是用于大气观测的，且讨论了光谱校准对测量结果的影响，这对于遥感数据的质量控制非常重要。
authors: Lukas Heizmann;Mathias Palm;Justus Notholt;Matthias Buschmann
title: Total power calibration in FTIR emission spectroscopy for finite interferograms
abstract:
Fourier transform infrared emission spectroscopy measures the infrared radiation originating from the thermal emission of the atmosphere. The measured interferograms are transformed into spectra via Fourier transformation. The established method for calibration is strictly speaking only valid for infinitely long interferograms. We quantify the errors caused by this idealization in a case study. 
 The NYAEM-FTS (Ny-Ålesund emission Fourier transform spectrometer) measures thermally emitted atmospheric radiation at a resolution of 0.08 cm−1 at Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard, since August 2019. To achieve this resolution, the spectrometer records interferograms in single-sided mode with a maximal optical path difference of 11.25 cm. The commonly used total power calibration procedure in FTIR (Fourier transform infrared) emission  spectroscopy first described by Revercomb et al. (1988) is strictly speaking only valid for double-sided, infinite interferograms. In order to correctly apply total power calibration to the NYAEM-FTS, we investigate the effect of interferogram truncation on calibrated mid-resolution emission spectra, describe the underlying theory, and quantify the errors in a case study. While application of the Revercomb formula might lead to large errors in the unequal-sided case, we show that one can obtain the same spectral estimate as from equal-sided interferograms. This is achieved by modifying Revercomb's method by incorporating a phase correction procedure using low-resolution phase spectra from the blackbody measurements. Since an error estimate requires idealized, quasi-infinite interferograms, we include a case study using simulated atmospheric and blackbody spectra with a line-by-line radiative transfer model, allowing e.g. for making informed decisions on retrieval window selection. For the mid-resolution use case with Arctic atmospheric conditions, we find that the effect of truncation on the spectral radiance measurement is generally well below 0.04 % in winter and 0.02 % in summer in spectral regions commonly used in trace gas retrievals with the AERI (Atmospheric Emitted Radiance Interferometer) and that the retrieval bands could be extended up to 1350 cm−1. At  higher wavenumbers where strong water vapor absorption lines in the blackbody spectra are present, the effect can be substantially larger. We also find that the method presented here reduces the maximal error in a band just below 1350 cm−1 from 0.39 % to 0.07 % in winter  and from 3.4 % to 0.6 % in summer for unequal-sided interferograms compared to the standard method. We recommend that such a quantitative analysis always be performed when applying total power calibration, since the quantitative effects are different for each use case.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术高度相关，因为它使用高分辨率低地球轨道（LEO）卫星图像来观测和评估飞机尾迹（contrails）的形成和早期演化。尾迹是大气成分分析的重要部分，对空气质量监测有直接影响。
authors: Thymen Woldhuis;Zebediah Engberg;Susanne Rohs;Vincent Meijer
title: Observing formation and early evolution of contrails formed by IAGOS aircraft using high-resolution LEO satellite imagery
abstract:
We introduce an algorithm that can find individual aircraft in high-resolution (10–30 m) satellite imagery to see whether they form contrails. We looked specifically for IAGOS (In-service Aircraft for a Global Observing System) aircraft which measure humidity: a key variable in predicting contrail formation and evolution. The final dataset consists of 543 IAGOS flights for which we know whether contrails form or not. We find excellent (98.3 %) agreement between these observations and predictions by a thermodynamic model of contrail formation. 
 Persistent contrails and contrail cirrus are estimated to be a major contributor to the climate impact of aviation. The mitigation of these impacts by means of technological or operational changes benefits from the ability to skillfully model the formation, evolution, and impacts of contrails. Although these models can be evaluated and improved by use of observations of contrails obtained from remote sensing instruments, these comparisons are hindered by uncertainty in the required meteorological data (such as relative humidity) and  limitations in the method of observation (such as younger contrails not being observable in geostationary satellite imagery). To address these challenges, we collocate aircraft equipped with in situ humidity sensors from the IAGOS fleet in high-resolution (10–30 m) satellite imagery obtained by instruments aboard the low Earth orbit (LEO) Sentinel-2 and Landsat missions. The resulting dataset consists of 543 IAGOS aircraft found in satellite imagery (51 % of which form contrails), which we use to evaluate predictions of contrail formation by the Schmidt–Appleman criterion (SAC) as well as predictions of contrail growth by the CoCiP model. When accounting for uncertainty in the IAGOS measurements of humidity and temperature, we find that the SAC correctly explains 98.3 % of the observations for the aircraft in the IAGOS fleet. Disagreement between predictions and observation increases when using meteorological data from the ERA5 reanalysis, with only 92.1 % of the observations being explained correctly. Out of the 195 annotated contrails, 48.2 % of these contrails were found to persist for longer than 10 s (approximately the jet phase) and 8.7 % longer than 120 s (approximately the vortex phase). The relative humidity with respect to ice is found to correlate most strongly with observed contrail lifetime, exhibiting an R2 value of 0.49 with the logarithm of contrail age. The observed horizontal growth during the jet and vortex phases is consistent with previous observations and contrail model results. Although the limited lifetimes of the annotated contrails prevent robust statistical conclusions for the dispersion phase, three example cases illustrate how the observed horizontal growth can be compared with contrail simulation results. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of high-resolution LEO satellites to create observational datasets for evaluating and improving models of contrail formation and early evolution.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它使用了Sentinel-2和Sentinel-1卫星数据来监测中国沿海湿地的范围和淹没频率。这些技术广泛应用于空气质量监测、卫星观测和大气成分分析等领域。
authors: Jintao Liang;Yong Zhang;Yi Wang;Chao Chen;Junfan Bao
title: CCWEM and CCWIF: 10 m Datasets of Coastal Wetland Extent and Inundation-Frequency Gradients across China
abstract:
We provide two open 10 m datasets describing China’s coastal wetlands in 2025. Together, they show both the maximum wetland extent and how tidal inundation varies within wetlands, offering a new national-scale spatial basis for wetland monitoring, ecological research, conservation, restoration, and coastal management. 
 Coastal wetlands are critical ecological spaces for coastal-zone management, with direct implications for wetland conservation, shoreline regulation, and nearshore spatial planning. Here, we present two complementary 10 m datasets for China's coastal wetlands in 2025: the China Coastal Wetland Extent Map (CCWEM) and the China Coastal Wetland Inundation Frequency Map (CCWIF). CCWEM delineates the maximum wetland extent along the Chinese coast, whereas CCWIF further characterizes internal inundation-frequency gradients within this extent. To generate CCWEM, we constructed a four-season semantic segmentation dataset based on multi-season Sentinel-2 observations and developed SeasonMamba, which integrates shared encoding, seasonal adaptive fusion, and pseudo-MSIC representation learning to achieve stable delineation of coastal wetlands under varying seasonal and tidal conditions. To generate CCWIF, the Chinese coast was divided into 58 tidal subregions to account for spatial heterogeneity in tidal environments, and a region-specific inundation-frequency estimation workflow was developed by integrating Sentinel-2 MNDWI time series with tide gauge observations. CCWEM mapped 8906.15 km² of coastal wetlands and achieved an overall accuracy of 94.07 %, with an F1 score of 94.83 % in low-tide boundary validation. Independent validation using Sentinel-1 observed water occurrence showed overall monotonic agreement with the CCWIF classes across all validation regions combined (Spearman's ρ = 0.756), supporting its ability to characterize relative inundation-frequency gradients. To our knowledge, CCWIF provides the first national-scale dataset describing coastal wetland inundation-frequency gradients across China. Together, CCWEM and CCWIF provide a consistent high-resolution spatial dataset for characterizing both the extent and internal hydrological structure of China's coastal wetlands, supporting coastal wetland monitoring, assessment, and management under complex tidal conditions.

explanation: 该论文研究的是东亚地区氮湿沉降的每日网格化数据集，结合了模拟、卫星降水数据和地面测量，这与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）密切相关，因为它涉及利用遥感数据（卫星降水数据）和模型融合来监测和量化大气污染物（氮沉降）的时空分布。
topic_words: ['nitrogen wet deposition', 'multisource observation-model fusion', 'satellite precipitation data', 'atmospheric nitrogen deposition']
authors: Nan Yang;Nuohang Liu;Baozhu Ge;Zhechen He;Yin Zhou;Danhui Xu;Zifa Wang
title: A daily gridded dataset of nitrogen wet deposition over East Asia for 2011 to 2016 based on multisource observation-model fusion
abstract:
We developed a daily dataset of nitrogen deposited by precipitation across East Asia for 2011–2016 at a resolution of 45 km. Combining simulations, satellite precipitation data and ground measurements improved agreement with observed daily nitrogen wet deposition. The dataset supports studies of short-lived nitrogen inputs to ecosystems and their contribution to total deposition. It also supports regional nitrogen budget analysis and model evaluation. 
 East Asia is a global hotspot of atmospheric nitrogen deposition, where episodic wet-deposition pulses can strongly affect ecosystem nutrient inputs and acidification. However, most datasets aggregate observations to monthly or annual scales, masking short-lived high-load deposition pulses from individual rainstorms and hindering the quantification of event-scale deposition dynamics. Here we develop a 45 km gridded daily dataset of oxidized and reduced nitrogen wet deposition over East Asia for 2011–2016. Ground-based measurements from the National Acid Deposition Monitoring Network (NADMN) and the Acid Deposition Monitoring Network in East Asia (EANET), satellite precipitation retrievals, and chemical transport simulations are integrated via a two-step framework. Precipitation adjustment constrains monthly deposition totals and reconstructs event-based daily deposition distributions, followed by measurement–model fusion to assimilate wet-deposition observations. Compared with the raw model output, the dataset reduces oxidized-nitrogen overestimation and better agreement with the observed spread of reduced-nitrogen wet deposition. Station-held-out validation shows improved identification of high-deposition days, with correct classification of the highest observed deposition quartile increasing by 12.7 and 20.8 percentage points for oxidized and reduced nitrogen, respectively. The daily dataset helps identify high-deposition periods and assess when and where short-lived nitrogen inputs occur and how much they contribute to cumulative deposition. It also supports regional nitrogen-budget analyses and model evaluation. However, uneven observational coverage and remaining errors in daily estimates warrant caution when interpreting individual events, particularly in sparsely monitored regions. The NetCDF data are available at https://doi.org/10.57760/sciencedb.015vd (Yang et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文使用卫星生物量地图和干扰地图结合国家森林调查数据，研究了法国森林的生长曲线、森林年龄和干扰趋势，这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测、卫星观测和大气成分分析高度相关。论文中明确提到了使用卫星数据（如FORMS-B和Landsat）来获取森林生物量和干扰信息，这些都是大气环境遥感技术的重要组成部分。
authors: Agnès Pellissier-Tanon;Yidi Xu;François Ritter;Nikola Besic;Philippe Ciais
title: Species- and region-specific growth curves, forest age (2020), and disturbance trends for French forests at 30 m resolution
abstract:
We created open data for mainland French forests to show, for different tree species and regions, how forests grow, how old they are, and how harvest and natural disturbances affect them. Combining satellite biomass and disturbance maps with national forest surveys, we map biomass growth with age, forest age for 2020, disturbance rates and biomass losses, and typical harvest ages. This helps explain the changing forest carbon sink and supports climate and management decisions. 
 Spatially explicit biomass growth curves data that jointly resolve tree species, stand age and disturbance regime are scarce, particularly at fine spatial resolutions. We present five consistent data products for metropolitan French forests around 2020, derived from a 30 m dominant-species map, the 30 m FORMS-B satellite above-ground biomass (AGB) map and the Landsat-based European Forest Disturbance Atlas: (1) 290 AGB growth curves for 28 species categories across 11 large ecological regions; (2) a 30 m forest age map for 2020 covering 17.01 Mha of forests, obtained by inverting these curves against the AGB map; (3) 3,752 harvest and natural disturbance rates and patch sizes, with their 1999–2024 trends; (4) 3,752 event-based disturbance severities (AGB loss per disturbed hectare); and (5) 1,874 rotation periods from National Forest Inventory (NFI) plot samples remeasurements. Products 3–5 cover 28 species categories across 86 small ecological regions. These cover the species×region combinations present in French forests, not the full combinatorial grid. Not all 28 species categories occur in every ecological region; the totals reflect strata with forest area only. All products include uncertainties and gap-filling flags. Growth curves match National Forest Inventory-derived curves for early growth (+12±15 %, 95 % CI) but give a higher asymptotic biomass (+22±18 %) and a later half-saturation year (+33±23 %), partly reflecting differences in the representation of age extremes, as NFI measurements exclude trees <7.5 cm in diameter and we aggregate stands >60 years into a single age class. The age map matches the NFI nationally aggregated age distribution (median offset −2 [−20 to +42] yr). The 2020 harvested area (44±6 kha) and the resulting AGB loss (2.5±0.3 MtC.yr−1) are of the same order as independent clear-cut estimates (62 kha from the NFI; ~3 MtC.yr−1 from satellite-mapped clear-cuts over 2018–2024). The Landsat disturbance product captures only stand-replacing and high severity events and underestimate selective logging and diffuse mortality. These products can be combined directly to model forest carbon dynamics at species and regional resolution. All data are openly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23499335 (Pellissier-Tanon et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文研究将机器学习组件与地球系统模型（ESMs）结合的方法，涉及气候预测和环境模拟，与大气环境遥感技术中的模型构建和数据分析密切相关。
authors: Alexis Barge;Julien Le Sommer;Andrea Storto;Sophie Valcke
title: Deploying machine learning components coupled to Earth  System Models with OASIS3-MCT (v6) and Eophis (v1.1)
abstract:
Scientists use programs, called Earth System Models, to study and predict climate. These models are based on physical theories but can be completed with AI tools. However, combining these tools with traditional models is difficult due to their different nature. Our research introduces a new method that connects these AI tools with existing climate models. We tested this method by integrating it with an ocean model. This work should help scientists explore new ways of making climate predictions. 
 The integration of machine learning (ML) components into Earth System Models (ESMs) holds significant potential for improving climate simulations, but it is often constrained by challenges related to interoperability, reproducibility, and computational efficiency. This paper presents a novel coupler-based approach that combines the OASIS3-MCT coupling library with Eophis, a high-performance Python library, to seamlessly deploy ML components in ESMs. By leveraging OASIS3-MCT’s robust communication infrastructure, Eophis abstracts the technical complexities of coupling, enabling users to integrate Python-based ML models or analytical parameterizations into geophysical simulations. Eophis provides a modular interface for defining data exchanges, synchronizing time steps, and supporting parallel communications, including advanced features such as halo construction for Convolutional Neural Networks and hybrid CPU/GPU execution. We evaluate this framework by coupling the NEMO4 ocean model with both ML-based and analytical parameterizations, demonstrating scalability, asynchronous execution, and flexible resource allocation. Benchmarking results show that this approach allows for deploying Python scripts in NEMO without affecting time-to-solution, provided extra computing resources are adequately allocated. The combination of OASIS3-MCT and Eophis offers a user-friendly solution for hybrid modelling, which facilitates the integration of ML components into ESM workflows.By lowering the barrier to hybrid modeling, this work facilitates the integration of ML components into ESM workflows. The combination of OASIS3-MCT and Eophis offers a practical solution for bridging the gap between ML and climate modeling, supporting innovation in Earth system science while maintaining reproducibility and ease of use.

explanation: 该论文主要关注海洋模型的模拟，特别是海岸带次微尺度不稳定现象，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）的直接相关性较弱。
authors: Kyle E. Hinson;Dylan R. Schlichting;Robert D. Hetland;Darren Engwirda;Katherine M. Smith;Mark R. Petersen;Kaila Uyeda
title: Towards high-fidelity simulations of coastal submesoscale baroclinic instabilities with MPAS-O (vE3SM3.0.0) – Part 1: Idealized experiments
abstract:
Physical dynamics of ocean flows at fine spatial scales are challenging for regional and global scale ocean models due to high computational effort associated with smaller grid cell sizes. We compared two ocean models: a regional model (ROMS; Regional Ocean Modeling System) and global model (MPAS-O; Model for Prediction Across Scales – Ocean) across a range of resolutions (10 km to 100 m) in an idealized domain, and found that their similarities may hold promise for future coupling between them. 
 Rapid advances in computational power over the past decade have enabled global, kilometer-scale simulations that realistically represent open-ocean submesoscale dynamics. However, the ability of global ocean models to represent coastal submesoscale dynamics – where flows are more heterogeneous and strongly shaped by coastlines, bathymetry, and buoyancy inputs – remains largely unexplored. This study is the first of two companion papers comparing coastal submesoscale processes representation in two models with very different numerical approaches: MPAS-O, an unstructured grid global ocean model, and ROMS, a structured grid regional model. This study is the first idealized evaluation of MPAS-O’s representation of coastal submesoscale dynamics using observed conditions in the Mississippi-Atchafalaya (M-A) River plume as a template for initial conditions, with the previously validated ROMS model serving as a benchmark. An important motivation for this study is to examine the suitability of models designed for global ocean simulations in reproducing energetic coastal flows. We compare statistical metrics based on flow invariants – total strain, relative vorticity, and divergence – as well as velocity gradients in frontal coordinates, across horizontal resolutions ranging from 10 km to 100 m within an idealized model domain. We find that the representation of submesoscale baroclinic instabilities is highly similar across all resolutions such that the impact of model choice is smaller than the choice of spatial grid resolution. We also compare numerical and physical mixing between models using online diagnostics based on discrete variance decay. We find that ROMS generally has more numerical mixing and less physical mixing than MPAS-O across all resolutions. Trends in numerical mixing likely arise from MPAS-O's flux-corrected transport tracer advection scheme, which exhibits a stronger variance-producing response relative to the MPDATA scheme used in the ROMS simulations. Trends in physical mixing likely arise from differences in each model’s configuration of the vertical mixing scheme (the K-Profile Parameterization). A companion paper extends this idealized model-model comparison to realistic simulations of the M-A River plume.

title: PROSWIN: Probabilistic Solar Wind Speed Forecasting Using Deep Distributional Regression From Solar Images
abstract: Accurately predicting fast solar wind conditions is challenging, as uncertainties are large and unquantified by traditional single‐value prediction models. In particular, the risks of high‐speed solar wind streams (HSSs), which can cause damage to technological infrastructure, cannot be reliably assessed without probabilistic forecasts. We present PROSWIN, a probabilistic machine learning model that forecasts the hourly solar wind speed (SWS) at Earth with a 4‐day lead time. The approach combines solar images and magnetograms using a deep neural network coupled to a distributional regression algorithm. Because standard error metrics underweight the relevance of HSS peaks, we further introduce the prediction score (PS), a model‐selection metric that jointly rewards timeline and HSS peak accuracy. On 14 years of data, our forecast achieves very well‐calibrated uncertainties (<1% average absolute coverage deviation). Using the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), a metric that assesses distributional accuracy, we obtain a timeline CRPS of 41.0 km/s, an HSS peak CRPS of 45.3 km/s, and a PS of 42.3 km/s. We find that the 171 Å channel is an important complement to the typically used 193 and 211 Å channels and that the PS for model selection improves the applicability of the model. Compared to selected models from the literature, ours is the only one that is accurate for both timeline and HSS peak values, rather than trading one off against the other. These results support the advantages of probabilistic over single‐value solar wind models. The introduced methods are also transferable to other forecasting problems.

title: Evolution of Summit Magma Pressure During the 2018 Caldera Collapse at Kīlauea Volcano
abstract: We utilized geodetic data from the 16 May to 4 August 2018 caldera collapse sequence to refine the geometries and pressure evolution of two summit reservoirs at Kīlauea volcano: the shallower Halema‘uma‘u (HMM) and deeper South Caldera (SC) reservoirs. We modeled magma reservoirs as pressurized spheroidal cavities and constrained reservoir geometries with Global Positioning System (GPS) and Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar displacements. Inverting high‐rate GPS and borehole tilt time series recovered time‐dependent reservoir pressure changes and caldera ring fault shear stress. During the collapse sequence, the HMM reservoir accommodated episodic, co‐collapse pressure increases of 1.9 MPa (median) and a net 5.8 MPa (median) decrease. Simultaneously, the SC reservoir underwent monotonic depressurization of 6.7 MPa (median). Negligible co‐collapse pressure changes in the SC reservoir imply it was not exclusively supplying magma to the eruption vent. These results provide a coherent view of magma reservoir pressure evolution during the 2018 eruption.

title: How Does Terrain Relief of the Tibetan Plateau and the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau Individually Modulate Summer Regional Hourly Extreme Precipitation in the Sichuan Basin, China?
abstract: The influence of terrain relief over the Tibetan Plateau (TP) and the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau on summer regional hourly extreme precipitation (RHEP) in the Sichuan Basin (SCB) under two dominant synoptic patterns remains poorly understood. Here, this study uses multi‐case Weather Research and Forecasting sensitivity experiments, in which the terrain relief of two plateaus is individually smoothed, to systematically investigate these modulation mechanisms. Terrain relief modulates low‐level flow and moisture, altering thermodynamic and dynamic processes of RHEP under different synoptic patterns. Under P1, featured by a westerly trough and a southwest vortex over western SCB, the terrain relief over the TP (Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau) prolongs the mean RHEP duration by 3.4 hr (0.6 hr) and increases the mean intensity by 0.38 mm hr−1 (0.24 mm hr−1) over the western SCB. The prolonged duration and heightened intensity of RHEP are driven by the intensification of the westerly trough and southwest vortex, a process triggered by enhanced atmospheric baroclinicity, low‐level convergence, and vertical‐motion forcing induced by terrain relief. Under P2, characterized by a westerly trough and a southwest vortex over central‐eastern SCB, the terrain relief over the TP prolongs the RHEP duration by 1.3 hr and increases the intensity by 0.07 mm hr−1 over eastern SCB through mechanisms similar to those under P1, but the weakened westerly winds over southeastern SCB limit the enhancement. In contrast, the terrain relief over the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau reduces the RHEP intensity by 0.32 mm hr−1 via strengthening anomalous northerly winds, blocking southwesterly moisture transport, weakening the westerly trough, and suppressing the southwest vortex.

title: Relationships Between Aerosols, Warm Clouds, and Meteorological Factors Associated With Environmental Conditions Derived From Multiyear ARM Observations
abstract: We derive new aspects between clouds, aerosols, and meteorological factors using latest observations. We analyze multiyear measurements of atmospheric physical properties including warm clouds and aerosols collected at Atmospheric Radiation Measurement continental and maritime facilities during 2016–2020 and 2015–2021, respectively. Diurnal variation of the aerosol optical depth (AOD) collocated with a neighboring cloud results from adjacent low tropospheric vertical wind shear (VWS725–925 hPa) due to aerosols originating from soils stirred up by enhanced turbulence at Southern Great Plains (SGP). There are similarities between seasons (summer or winter) and surface wind directions (north or south) with respect to the relations between aerosol‐cloud, cloud‐cloud, and cloud‐meteorological factor at the maritime Eastern North Atlantic (ENA) site, as well as with respect to diurnal variations of clouds, aerosols, and meteorological factors at both sites. Particularly, there is a strong similarity in the diurnal variation of convective available potential energy at SGP. At ENA over the ocean, aerosol‐cloud‐meteorological relationships, such as the relationship between cloud top height and AOD can be interpreted in terms of a temperature inversion at the top of the marine boundary layer. Some cloud properties, for example, the cloud thickness responds as “V”‐ or “Λ”‐shapes to the aerosol thickness at SGP and vice versa at ENA. There are reciprocal seasonal variations in dependence of cloud properties, for example, cloud extinction coefficient on aerosol scale height between SGP and ENA. The aerosol‐cloud horizontal configuration (i.e., which side of the cloud an aerosol profile is located on) can affect the relations between aerosol‐cloud properties, particularly the sign of linear trend slope in aerosol‐cloud relationships.

title: An Investigation of the Characteristics of Indian Summer Monsoon Low‐Pressure Systems Under Stratospheric Aerosol Geoengineering
abstract: Monsoon Low‐Pressure Systems (LPSs) that govern the rainfall of the Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) contribute more than half of its rainfall and extreme rainfall events. In this study, we explore how LPS activity changes under greenhouse warming and Stratospheric Aerosol Intervention (SAI) using simulations from the fully coupled CESM2.1.3 climate model. We simulate three different climate scenarios: CTRL (control climate), 2XCO2 (doubling of CO2 $C{O}_{2}$), and UNIFORM (a globally uniform stratospheric sulfate aerosol forcing superimposed on the 2XCO2 climate). In the 2XCO2 simulation, the global mean surface temperature increases by 3.22 K, accompanied by a weakened ISM circulation, reflected in a weaker Walker circulation, reduced vertical zonal wind shear, and weaker low‐level Barotropic Shear (BS). However, despite 6% increase in the All‐India rainfall (AIR) due to increased atmospheric water vapor, the total count of LPSs and LPS days decreases by approximately 9%–14%, but the systems on average produce stronger rainfall and extreme rainfall events in central and northern India. The UNIFORM scenario restores global mean surface temperature within 0.03 K of CTRL and partially revives monsoon circulation, BS, and recovers LPS frequency and spatial distribution toward CTRL levels. However, this aerosol experiment forcing suppresses the hydrological cycle, decreasing atmospheric moisture and AIR by 3.82% compared to CTRL (9.28% relative to 2XCO2), along with weakened LPS rainfall and extreme rainfall events. In summary, while uniform SAI can partially revive monsoon circulation and LPS activity, it simultaneously suppresses the thermodynamically driven increase in rainfall and extreme rainfall events associated with greenhouse warming.

abstract:
Evaluations of AI models predicting disease-causing single nucleotide variants reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is inflated by mixing variant types, e.g. canonical splice and 5’ UTR variants. The authors introduce a stratified benchmark to accurately identify the most robust models. 
 Recent studies have reported unprecedented accuracy predicting pathogenic variants across the genome, including in noncoding regions, using large deep-learning models trained on vast genomic data. To verify and understand the basis of these reports, we systematically evaluated the prediction accuracy of frontier models over single-nucleotide variants, focusing on general models capable of scoring multiple variant types across coding or noncoding regions. Our evaluations reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is severely inflated by mixing variant categories with different baseline prevalences of pathogenic variants. We constructed a benchmark stratified by variant type to identify the best-performing models for each genomic context, determine where reliable predictions remain out of reach, and establish rigorous standards to guide future evaluations. title: IDPForge: deep learning of proteins with global and local regions of disorder
abstract:
Intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDPs/IDRs) are defined by diverse structural ensembles. We present IDPForge that exploits a transformer protein language diffusion model to create all-atom IDP and IDR ensembles that maintain folded domains with options to conform to experimental data. 
 Although machine learning has transformed protein structure prediction of folded protein ground states with remarkable accuracy, intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDPs/IDRs) are defined by diverse and dynamical structural ensembles that are predicted with low confidence by algorithms such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold. We present a machine learning method, IDPForge (Intrinsically Disordered Protein, FOlded and disordered Region GEnerator), that exploits a transformer protein language diffusion model to create all-atom IDP ensembles and IDR ensembles that maintains the folded domains. IDPForge does not require sequence-specific training, back transformations from coarse-grained representations, nor ensemble reweighting. The created IDP/IDR conformational ensembles show good agreement with both NMR and SAXS solution experimental data, and options for biasing with experimental restraints are available if desired. IDPForge with these diverse capabilities facilitates integrative and structural studies for proteins that contain intrinsic disorder, and is available as an open source resource for general use. title: Ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome
abstract:
The genetics of restless legs syndrome have mostly been studied in European populations. Here, the authors perform a multi-ancestry genetic study of the condition, revealing differences in genetic risk across populations with different ancestries. 
 Restless legs syndrome is a neurological disorder that disrupts sleep and quality of life, but its genetics have mostly been studied in individuals of European ancestry. Here, we perform GWAS of restless legs syndrome using data from individuals of African, Latin American, and European ancestry, followed by a multi-ancestry meta-analysis. We leverage biobank-based cohorts that established RLS diagnosis using validated clinical criteria, allowing for precise phenotypic characterization. We perform ancestry-specific association studies and post-GWAS analyses to prioritize candidate genes. Our analyses reveal ancestry differences in the genetics of restless legs syndrome. At the MEIS1 and BTBD9 loci, lead variants showed lower allele frequencies and did not reach genome-wide significance in African ancestry. We identify ancestry-specific and shared risk loci, including novel associations near GYPC/TEX51 and PRIMA1 in African ancestry and ISX in Latin American ancestry. The European meta-analysis identifies 11 additional loci and replicates 50 previously reported associations. The combined multi-ancestry analysis finds ten new loci. This multi-ancestry study broadens the genetic understanding of restless legs syndrome, and the absence or reduced frequency of key European restless legs syndrome alleles in individuals of African ancestry provides insights into known epidemiological differences. title: A multilamellar organelle for chemosymbiosis in an aplacophoran mollusc adapted to anoxic cold seep sediment
abstract:
Animals living in the deep sea often form symbiotic partnerships with chemosynthetic bacteria. Here authors discover a multilamellar organelle in the worm-mollusc Chaetoderma shenloong containing bacteria and name it dracosphera (‘dragon ball’). 
 Symbiosis with chemoautotrophic bacteria has evolved in many animal lineages inhabiting reducing habitats such as hydrothermal vents, allowing these holobionts to thrive in dark biospheres. In certain cases, the symbionts have become intracellular, residing within specialised bacteriocytes. Although the integration of microbial symbionts with eukaryotic cells varies across known animals, no specialised organelle dedicated to chemosynthesis has been identified. Here, we report a mode of symbiosis where sulphur-oxidising bacteria are cultured within spherical multilamellar compartments ( ~ 12 μm) in the cold-seep aplacophoran mollusc Chaetoderma shenloong. This organelle, which we name ‘dracosphera’, is ubiquitous within the hypertrophied and intricately reticulate digestive gland of C. shenloong, which has otherwise lost most of its gut. Given that the symbionts are microaerobic and the host resides in anoxic sediments tens of centimetres below the surface, the dracosphera may minimise oxygen diffusion to the bacteria, akin to mechanisms observed in microbial diazotrophs and termite hindguts, as supported by our genomic and spatial transcriptomic analyses. Hypoxia is known to induce radical adaptations in meiofauna, exemplified by the acquisition of hydrogenosomes. Our discovery of similar adaptations in C. shenloong provides insights into the evolution of such organelles in larger animals. title: Process-dependent shifts in conspecific negative density dependence during boreal forest succession
abstract:
Conspecific negative density dependence may maintain diversity, but its role during succession is unclear. This study shows that changes depend on demographic processes and species abundance rather than following a uniform community-wide trend. 
 Conspecific negative density dependence (CNDD)—the stronger negative effects of conspecific than heterospecific neighbours on plant demographic performance—is a key process proposed to stabilize forest diversity, yet how it changes during succession remains poorly understood. Using a 25-year spatially explicit dataset from 148 post-fire plots in boreal forests, we show that species richness increases with stand age and that CNDD varies in process- and abundance-dependent ways across recruitment, survival, and growth. Plot-level CNDD shows no significant change with stand age in recruitment or survival, but mean relative effects are generally stronger for recruitment, and CNDD shifts from destabilizing to stabilizing for growth as stands mature. Species-level CNDD is strongly associated with species abundance, with rare species consistently experiencing stronger CNDD in recruitment and growth, whereas common species tend toward neutral or destabilizing effects. For survival, by contrast, CNDD is stronger in common than in rare species. These abundance-related differences remain broadly consistent across stand development, except in recruitment, where CNDD intensifies in rare species but remains consistently weak or near-neutral in common species. This shifting balance of density-dependent pressures highlights succession-driven trade-offs as central to species coexistence and increases in diversity in disturbance-driven forests. This study shows that changes depend on demographic processes and species abundance rather than following a uniform community-wide trend.

abstract:
Hydrogel actuators have potential in a range of applications, but combining rapid actuation and complex deformation is challenging. Here, the authors report a lamellar confined assembly polymerisation strategy for preparing programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels. 
 Inspired by organisms capable of adaptive morphological regulation, hydrogel actuators with softness and large deformability are attractive for biomedical devices and information encryption, yet remain limited by the lack of hierarchically oriented structures simultaneously enabling rapid actuation and high-order complex deformation. Here, we report a multiscale lamellar-confined assembly polymerization strategy for fabricating synchronous programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels with hierarchically periodic lamellar-cellular structure. Owing to the periodic asymmetric stresses that amplify deformation and hierarchical porous channels that accelerate water transport, the obtained hydrogel exhibits large three-dimensional deformation with the rapidest recovery speed of 112.5°/s among the reported thermo-responsive hydrogels, facilitating programmable shape morphing by orchestrating localized curvature. Furthermore, a spatial orientation-patterning strategy is developed to precisely regulate the site-specific arrangement of lamellar-cellular structures for diverse cooperative sophisticated deformations at high speed. Importantly, the highly oriented architecture endows the hydrogel with tunable birefringence, enabling a dynamic encryption platform that couples programmable deformation with information encoding. This work provides a flexible structural strategy for preparing hydrogels with biomimetic dynamic information encryption. Hydrogel actuators have potential in a range of applications, but combining rapid actuation and complex deformation is challenging. Here, the authors report a lamellar confined assembly polymerisation strategy for preparing programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels.

title: Intruding delta waves during REM sleep are associated with tau, amyloid, and forgetting in aging
abstract:
Desel et al. report that memory loss in aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow delta waves during REM sleep. This shift correlates with amyloid and tau burden, marking a REM sleep signature of impaired memory consolidation. 
 Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep degrades with age, and more severely in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). REM sleep comprises about twenty percent of adult sleep, alternates between phasic and tonic periods, and includes delta waves (1-4 Hz) in two forms: fast sawtooth waves and slower, NREM-like waves, whose expression dynamically varies across REM periods. Yet, the functional relevance of these REM sleep delta waves remains unknown. Here, using two independent cohorts, we show that aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow NREM-like delta waves, particularly during phasic REM sleep - a period typically marked by high cortical activation. Beyond chronological age, this shift is associated with amyloid-β and tau burden, suggesting that AD pathology is associated with REM-specific oscillatory patterns. Furthermore, this shift in REM oscillations is linked to impaired overnight memory consolidation, independent of NREM sleep quality. Moreover, variation in APOE alleles, a major genetic risk factor for AD, was independently associated with a reduction in fast sawtooth wave density, thereby linking a genetic predisposition for AD to these specific REM microstructural changes. These findings identify a signature of memory decline in aging and implicate REM sleep as a distinct vulnerable substrate through which AD pathology may impair brain function. Desel et al. report that memory loss in aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow delta waves during REM sleep. This shift correlates with amyloid and tau burden, marking a REM sleep signature of impaired memory consolidation.

title: Atmospheric stabilization of the East Antarctic ice sheet under warming
abstract:
The long-term response of the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets to warming is often studied using ice-only simulations. Here the authors use a coupled ice–atmosphere–ocean model and find that East Antarctica remains stable even under higher warming because changes in atmospheric circulation increase precipitation sensitivity. 
 Most coupled Earth system models do not include fully interactive ice sheets, introducing uncertainty in future projections of polar climate and global sea level. To this end, we conduct 100,000-year-long simulations for different CO2 conditions using the community Earth system model coupled to the bihemispheric Penn State University ice sheet–ice shelf model. Whereas global warming exceeding 2 °C above pre-industrial conditions and related subsurface ocean warming lead to the millennial-scale disintegration of the West Antarctic ice sheet, the East Antarctic ice sheet shows a much greater resilience, even at 10 °C or more of warming. The simulations reveal that a moister and cloudier atmosphere over Antarctica, with southward-shifted westerlies, increases snow accumulation and reduces shortwave radiation. For Greenland, a 6 °C threshold above pre-industrial levels is identified. Capturing the balance of ocean- and atmosphere-driven ablation and accumulation processes in coupled climate–ice-sheet models will improve projections of long-term sea-level rise. Here the authors use a coupled ice–atmosphere–ocean model and find that East Antarctica remains stable even under higher warming because changes in atmospheric circulation increase precipitation sensitivity.

title: Disentangling dynamic and thermodynamic pathways reveals nonlocal winter climate responses to historical land use and land cover change
abstract:
Disentangling dynamic and thermodynamic pathways reveals nonlocal winter climate responses to historical land use and land cover change 
 Historical land use and land cover change (LULCC) can influence both nearby and distant climates through land–atmosphere interactions, yet its non-local climatic impacts remain poorly constrained. One possible explanation is that previous studies conflated non-local effects arising from distinct physical processes. Here we used CMIP6 models to separate the influences of large-scale circulation, thermodynamic advection, and local surface energy balance in winter surface air temperature responses to historical LULCC. We show that circulation-induced changes generate weak but significant warming over the Canada–Greenland region, with negligible signals elsewhere. After removing this dynamic component, a widespread and robust thermodynamic cooling signal emerges in the mid-latitudes due to advection, with magnitudes of ~0.3 K across hotspot regions and local areas cooling up to 1 K. Local energy contributions are smaller, mainly linked to albedo and downward longwave radiation changes. This process-based attribution significantly reduces inter-model spread, advances the mechanistic understanding of land–atmosphere interactions, and highlights the importance of considering non-local climate effects in assessments of land-use change and climate mitigation strategies.

title: Skillful subseasonal-to-seasonal ensemble forecasting with a multi-sphere coupled probabilistic model
abstract:
Skillful subseasonal-to-seasonal ensemble forecasting with a multi-sphere coupled probabilistic model 
 Accurate subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) prediction is critical for disaster mitigation under accelerating climate change, yet remains challenging due to complex multi-sphere interactions and intrinsic atmospheric uncertainty. Here we present TianXing-S2S, a multi-sphere coupled probabilistic deep learning model for global S2S ensemble forecasting. TianXing-S2S first encodes diverse multi-sphere predictors into a compact latent space, then employs a diffusion model to generate daily ensemble forecasts. A novel coupling module based on optimal transport (OT) is incorporated in the denoiser to optimize the interactions between atmospheric and multi-sphere boundary conditions. Across key atmospheric variables, TianXing-S2S outperforms both the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) S2S system and FuXi-S2S in 45-day daily-mean ensemble forecasts at 1.5° × 1.5° resolution. Our model improves the prediction of extreme events including heat waves and anomalous precipitation, with multi-sphere coupling identified as a key contributor. Furthermore, we demonstrate that TianXing-S2S can generate stable rollout forecasts up to 180 days, suggesting its potential as a useful framework for probabilistic S2S prediction under a changing climate.

title: Large intraplate earthquakes on an extinct oceanic plate reveal fracture zone reactivation
abstract:
Cessation of plate-boundary activity at oceanic fracture zones does not imply mechanical quiescence, these can be reactivated under present-day stress conditions, shown through analysis of two earthquakes that occurred in 2025 within the former Phoenix Plate in the Drake Passage region. 
 Oceanic fracture zones, the inactive traces of former transform faults, are often considered tectonically inactive once relative plate motion across them ceases. However, their long-term mechanical behavior and role in intraplate deformation remain poorly understood. Here, we analyze two earthquakes of Mw 7.5 and Mw 7.6 that occurred about 15 km and 49 days apart in 2025 within the Phoenix Plate, along a structure spatially consistent with a former oceanic transform fault in the Drake Passage region. These events indicate that such structures remain lithosphere-scale  zones of mechanical weakness and can be reactivated under present-day stress conditions. We propose here that inherited fault geometry and regional far-field stresses associated with Scotia–Antarctic plate interactions collectively promote strain localization on these presumed fossil structures. Our results indicate that the cessation of plate-boundary activity does not imply mechanical quiescence, and that oceanic fracture zones represent long-lived zones of intraplate weakness that can both host large-magnitude earthquakes and facilitatevolcanic emplacement, as shown by a seismic reflection profile crossing the fracture zone near the earthquake epicenters. This structure acts as a lithosphere-scale tear fault within the slow subducting Phoenix slab beneath the South Shetland continental block. This behavior has implications for the mechanical evolution of oceanic lithosphere and for the interpretation of intraplate seismicity near extinct plate boundaries. Cessation of plate-boundary activity at oceanic fracture zones does not imply mechanical quiescence, these can be reactivated under present-day stress conditions, shown through analysis of two earthquakes that occurred in 2025 within the former Phoenix Plate in the Drake Passage region.

title: Global warming and the Pacific Decadal Oscillation drive seasonally varying increases in extreme fire weather over the southwestern US
abstract:
Wildfire risk in the western United States increases during winter and spring in response to global warming, while summer fire weather extremes follow the variation of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, as revealed by analysis based on long-term reanalysis. 
 Wildfire activity has increased across the western United States (US), with evidence linking these trends to anthropogenic climate forcing. Here, we analyze the frequency, intensity, and drivers of fire weather extremes in the southwestern US over the past 83 years. These extremes exhibit strong seasonality: wintertime changes align with long-term warming trends, while summertime variations are dominated by decadal fluctuations modulated by the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO). Fire risk has increased steadily during December–May, outside the traditional fire season, primarily due to rising temperatures and declining relative humidity (RH). In contrast, summertime fire risk, largely governed by humidity, follows a roughly V-shaped trajectory, decreasing from 1940-1980 and then rising from 1981-2022, in close alignment with decadal shifts in the PDO. Although Earth system models reliably capture temperature-related changes, they underestimate interdecadal variability in humidity, manifested by a weak representation of the observed PDO–RH relationship and low-RH extremes in summer. Wildfire risk in the western United States increases during winter and spring in response to global warming, while summer fire weather extremes follow the variation of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, as revealed by analysis based on long-term reanalysis.

title: Diversified cropping rotation increases soil carbon sequestration via fungal-mediated necromass production and mineral association
abstract:
Crop diversification increased soil organic carbon by 10–15%, boosted microbial growth and carbon-use efficiency, shifted communities toward fungi, and raised mineral-associated carbon by 48–69%, based on a 43-year field trial and community transplantation assays. 
 Crop diversification boosts soil organic carbon (SOC) storage, yet uncertainty persists regarding its effects on molecular SOC composition. Using a 43-year field trial in fluvo-aquic soil, we contrasted conventional wheat-rice (ConCrop) versus diversified rice/wheat – cotton/barley – maize/faba bean rotations (DivCrop). We demonstrated DivCrop elevated SOC by 9.6% (0–15 cm) and 15% (15–30 cm). DivCrop alleviated C-nitrogen co-limitation, stimulating 150% greater microbial growth and 47% higher C use efficiency. This coincided with restructured microbial communities shifting toward fungal dominance and increased functional capacity. Community transplantation assays confirmed increased adaptation for efficient C processing. Diversification accelerated lignin decomposition (plant-derived C reduced by 19–35%) and redirecting C flow toward fungal necromass (20–44% of total microbial necromass). Consequently, mineral-associated organic C increased 48–69%, with short-term formation efficiency rising 98–160% via reactive iron oxide interactions. Diversification thus shifts plant-derived recalcitrance towards mineral-stabilized microbial products in low-SOC soils, reshaping SOC composition toward climate-resilient agriculture. Crop diversification increased soil organic carbon by 10–15%, boosted microbial growth and carbon-use efficiency, shifted communities toward fungi, and raised mineral-associated carbon by 48–69%, based on a 43-year field trial and community transplantation assays.

title: Integrating local and landscape management promotes biodiversity, multifunctionality and yields in tropical agroforests
abstract:
Amazonian cacao agroforests can jointly sustain biodiversity and yields when shade-tree structure and surrounding tree cover are optimized, with vertebrate-mediated pest control doubling yields, based on integrated assessments of biodiversity, ecosystem services, and production. 
 Reconciling food production and biodiversity conservation requires socio-ecologically viable agroecosystems. To meet this goal, tropical agroforestry must balance yield-biodiversity trade-offs through local and landscape-level management. By integrating assessments of multi-taxa diversity, biocontrol, pollination, crop pests, soil fertility, microclimate, and yield in Amazonian cacao agroforests, we identified ecological-economic synergies. Yield gains were not associated with species loss. Instead, agroforests with high spatial and vertical shade-tree heterogeneity embedded in landscapes combining 30–35% forest cover and 40–45% of other arboreal habitats (e.g., orchards/agroforests) achieved the highest biodiversity and yields. In these landscapes, flying-vertebrate-mediated arthropod suppression doubled cacao yields. Increasing agroforest shade-tree cover from ≈15% to ≈80% yielded a four-fold rise in cacao fruit-set, tripled soil potassium and enhanced thermal buffering. But light limitation, rather than pest pressure, reduced harvestable yields above 30% shade-tree cover. Our findings demonstrate that combined agroforest-level and landscape-scale management can align biodiversity conservation and economic returns in tropical landscapes. Amazonian cacao agroforests can jointly sustain biodiversity and yields when shade-tree structure and surrounding tree cover are optimized, with vertebrate-mediated pest control doubling yields, based on integrated assessments of biodiversity, ecosystem services, and production.

title: Non-analog environments supported early Homo sapiens in southern Africa 200 000 years ago
abstract:
Early Homo sapiens in South Africa experienced contrasting, non‑analogous environments shaped by shifting hydrology and vegetation, based on plant biomarker isotope records and revised dating of Middle-Pleistocene fossil sites, which provides context for hominin adaptive strategies 
 In our species’ evolutionary history, the type of environments in which we evolved can provide crucial details about early human adaptive capacities. Such environments might not exist under current climatic and ecological conditions. Reconstructing palaeohydrology and vegetation using multiple proxies at human fossil sites in South Africa provides insights into local conditions at a high level of detail. This paper presents a plant n-alkane stable isotope record for Florisbad and Lombard’s Drift, which is anchored by new luminescence ages that revise the age for the Florisbad human cranium. We observe contrasting, non-analog plant environments during the Middle and Late Pleistocene by combining multiple lines of evidence to better understand the different environments that early Homo sapiens experienced. It also provides the foundation to evaluate their cultural adaptation strategies through time. title: Decoder-FFPE-seq enables sensitive, genome-wide spatial transcriptomics of archival tissues at single-cell resolution
abstract: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue–compatible spatial transcriptomics (ST) is transforming biology and histopathology, but achieving high sensitivity, genome-wide coverage, single-cell resolution, and researcher accessibility remains challenging. To address these challenges, we here present a dendrimeric DNA coordinate barcoding design for FFPE tissue–adapted spatial RNA sequencing (Decoder-FFPE-seq) by integrating RNA-to-DNA probe conversion with blotting-assisted barcoding. Decoder-FFPE-seq provides single-cell resolution with a >2.6-fold sensitivity increase in whole-transcriptome mouse brain and archived human sample profiling over existing platforms, resolving potential cellular identity of low-abundance genes, finer tissue architecture, and capturing an epithelial-mesenchymal transition–associated signature for prognostic value. With expanded probe libraries, Decoder-FFPE-seq captures long noncoding and viral RNAs, revealing their spatial coregulatory networks with messenger RNAs in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCCs). In an OSCC immunotherapy cohort, two CD8+T cell subpopulations were respectively identified in pre- and postchemoimmunotherapy samples, potentially linked to treatment response. Decoder-FFPE-seq establishes a robust, high-resolution, and accessible framework for sensitive ST profiling of archival tissues in fundamental and translational studies.

title: Graph-based pangenome analysis uncovers structural and functional impacts of allopolyploidization events
abstract: The emergence of graph pangenomes has advanced the study of structural variants (SVs) across diverse species, yet the impact of complex ploidy on SV landscapes remains poorly explored.Brettanomyces bruxellensis, a yeast shaped by multiple allopolyploidization events, offers a compelling model due to its well-characterized genomic and phenotypic diversity. Here, we integrated subgenome-resolved assemblies with population-scale genomic and transcriptomic datasets to characterize SV distribution and functional impact at the species level. Leveraging a reference graph pangenome, we detected 5972 unique SVs across 1060 isolates. Allopolyploid genomes harbored significantly more SVs (320 on average) than diploids (116), reflecting hybridization’s extensive impact on genome architecture. Functional association analysis revealed that 27.5% of SVs locally influence gene expression. Furthermore, a subset of SVs originating from ancestral divergence between subgenomes (hybridization-associated SVs) formed hotspots of structural diversity and disproportionately affect gene expression, with larger effect sizes than other SVs. These findings underscore allopolyploidization as a driver of structural and functional genomic diversification, highlighting the value of graph-based approaches in dissecting complex genome evolution.

title: A nematic framework for sprouting angiogenesis
abstract: Sprouting angiogenesis is critical for embryogenesis, wound healing, and tumor growth. Here, we show that the liquid crystal framework, which has recently been leveraged to study various morphogenetic events, provides unique insight into angiogenic sprouting. In response to vascular endothelial growth factor, a potent proangiogenic factor, endothelial cells cultured on the surfaces of soft collagen hydrogels form elongated cell streams that coexist with more polygonal cell regions. Angiogenic sprouting initiates preferentially at cell stream tips, where nematic order gradients are most pronounced. We demonstrate that cell streams are associated with large traction forces that lead to three-dimensional deformations of the underlying hydrogel and that stream formation results from a delicate balance between microtubule polymerization and actomyosin contractility. Last, we show that active control of nematic order allows modulation of sprout formation, highlighting the key role of endothelial cell orientation gradients in angiogenic sprouting and paving the way for new therapeutic avenues.

title: Robust pan-junctional reinforcement preserves the gut epithelial barrier under mechanical stress
abstract: Epithelia are specialized tissue barriers that safeguard the organism’s internal milieu from the external environment, a function critically dependent on intercellular junctions. In the colon, this barrier is repeatedly challenged by mechanical distension from feces, but it is unknown whether and how the colon adapts to this stress, which could otherwise compromise barrier integrity. Here, we show that feces-mediated mechanical distension triggers coordinated remodeling at cell and tissue scales, consistent with a mechanoadaptative response. This response includes recruitment of junctional proteins at all three types of adhesive cell-cell junctions (tight junctions, adherens junctions, and desmosomes). We identified protein-specific temporal profiles of junctional enrichment during distension, with ZO-1, E-cadherin, desmocollin 2, and plakoglobin exhibiting sustained junctional enrichment, whereas desmoplakin and keratin 8 showed progressive accumulation peaking at 15 min of distension. Distension was also accompanied by perijunctional recruitment and activation of nonmuscle myosin II (NMMII). Through genetic, pharmacological, and mechanical perturbations, we demonstrated that NMMII activation is required for epithelial mechanoadaptation. This process depends on extracellular calcium availability and mechanosensitive ion channel activity, supporting a role for calcium-dependent mechanosensitive signaling in NMMII-mediated junctional reinforcement. Loss of NMMII function impaired the junctional response to distension across all three junctional complexes, including desmosomes, resulting in disorganized junctions and barrier breach. Together, our findings uncover a robust physiological mechano-adaptive response of the adult colonic epithelium to an extrinsic mechanical stress, whereby coordinated reinforcement of all junctional complexes, requiring myosin II activity and calcium-dependent mechanosensitive signaling, preserves intestinal barrier integrity.

title: Chirality-selective second-harmonic response with Floquet engineering
abstract: Symmetry breaking profoundly influences the macroscopic physical properties of materials. For instance, inversion symmetry breaking in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides enables the emergence of chiral selection rules, featuring distinct optical chirality-selective electronic properties. Here, we demonstrate ultrafast, coherent manipulation of chirality-selective nonlinear optics in monolayer molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) through time-reversal symmetry breaking via Floquet engineering. By using sub-bandgap, circularly polarized ultrafast optical pulses, we introduce nondegenerate, chirality-selective optical Stark and Bloch-Siegert shifts. This approach effectively lifts the energy degeneracy, leading to pronounced chirality-selective second-harmonic generation. Furthermore, we reveal that the Floquet-engineered chirality-selective states can be finely tuned using optical parameters such as intensity and chirality. Our results show a method for manipulating the energy degree of freedom, paving the way for ultrafast nonlinear photonics.

title: RNA binding by ADARs prevents RNA interference from attacking self-produced dsRNA
abstract: The ability of an organism to distinguish between self and foreign double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) is central to eliciting an immune response when needed while preventing autoimmunity. UsingCaenorhabditis elegans, we investigated the interplay between two host pathways that regulate dsRNA expression and function, adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing by adenosine deaminases that act on RNA (ADARs), and RNA interference (RNAi). We found that the number of small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) targeting edited genes is significantly up-regulated in ADAR mutant animals. In addition, despite an almost complete depletion of primary siRNAs generated from editing sites in wild-type animals, secondary siRNAs are generated from edited transcripts, suggesting that ADARs antagonize only the first step of RNAi processing. We show that ADARs interfere with the efficacy of exogenous RNAi in vivo, likely to prevent trans-silencing, and provide evidence that ADR-2 binding to dsRNA is required for efficient RNAi suppression. This work sheds light on how RNA editing safeguards self-dsRNAs against immune recognition and by-product degradation.

title: Monsoon zonal seesaw: Development of the South Asian monsoon aridified North Africa in the Cenozoic
abstract: North Africa experienced a pronounced transition from humid to arid conditions during the early Cenozoic. Meanwhile, the South Asian monsoon underwent substantial intensification, largely driven by the uplift of the Himalayan-Tibetan Plateau. Here, we demonstrate that the two events, which greatly shaped the paleoenvironment and modern regional climate, are not independent responses to paleogeography changes; rather, the former is primarily driven by the latter through the monsoon-desert mechanism, in which South Asian monsoon diabatic heating produces large-scale subsidence and aridity over North Africa. Using multiple ensembles of paleoclimate simulations and a model for the atmospheric response to imposed diabatic heating, we show that the intensification and poleward shift of Asian monsoon rainfall each make comparable contributions to the aridification of North Africa. Our findings identify a persistent dynamical pathway linking the South Asian and North African monsoons and suggest that it played a major role in early Cenozoic North African aridification, while its climatic expression at other times depended on the relative strengths of competing forcings.

title: Enhanced room-temperature spin transport in a deuterated molecular single crystal
abstract: Achieving high-efficiency spin transport at room temperature remains a central challenge in spintronics. Molecular single crystals are ideal candidates for addressing this challenge because their highly ordered lattices and uniform transport pathways intrinsically suppress spin scattering and enable long spin lifetimes. However, integrating these intrinsic advantages into practical devices has remained challenging, primarily because molecular single crystals are extremely fragile during device fabrication. Here, we design a molecular single-crystal system with uniform spin-transport pathways and suppressed spin-relaxation channels, resulting in a substantially enhanced room-temperature spin lifetime, as confirmed by both theoretical analysis and experimental characterizations. By applying a damage-free crystal-handling method with an optimized electrode-transfer technique, we fabricate high-quality single-crystal spintronic devices and achieve a spin-transport efficiency of 15.17% at room temperature, nearly twice the previous benchmark (∼8%). This work establishes a generalizable strategy for designing long-spin-lifetime molecular spintronic materials and demonstrates the practical viability of molecular single crystals as a platform for efficient room-temperature spin transport.

title: Evidence of active whole-genome doubling (WGD) subclones in non-WGD tumors
abstract: Whole-genome doubling (WGD) occurs frequently in human cancer and influences tumor evolution, metastasis, and treatment response. Here, we integrate bulk, single-cell, and spatial data to dissect the subclonal dynamics of WGD. Single-cell data analysis shows that WGD cells are prevalent even in tumors that are classified as non-WGD (nWGD). WGD subclones actively acquire somatic copy number alterations as they expand, suggesting ongoing evolution. We developed and rigorously validated a gene expression–based method, WAGES, to map WGD cell clonal fraction in bulk tumors. Applying WAGES to nWGD tumors, we reveal genomic correlates includingTP53mutations and chromosomal instability that are consistent with the presence of WGD subclones. Clinically, WAGES scores are strongly correlated with tumor metastatic potential, response to treatments including chemotherapy and immunotherapy, and patient prognosis. These findings reveal widespread WGD subclones in nWGD tumors and demonstrate their substantial impact on cancer evolution and therapeutic outcomes.
