title: A soft wireless bioelectronic patch for noninvasive modulation of cavernosal microenvironment in diabetic erectile dysfunction
abstract: Diabetes mellitus–induced erectile dysfunction is difficult to reverse due to long-term impairment of cavernosal microenvironment. Conventional oral or intracavernosal injection therapies suffer from poor targeting, uneven drug distribution, and potential complications. Here, we propose a soft, wireless electronic patch for treating erectile dysfunction (SWEED) in diabetes mellitus, which enables safe, noninvasive, and controllable modulation of penile microenvironment. With its “microelectrode–drug reservoir–nanopore” configuration, SWE intensifies local electrical field nanoscopically and achieves uniform transdermal drug delivery. Through the enhanced local delivery of prostaglandin E1 (PGE1), SWEED demonstrates high efficiency in promoting the expression of vascular factors for endothelial repair and enhancing cavernosal blood perfusion. In both in vitro and in vivo settings, the platform achieves vascular regeneration and functional recovery comparable to clinical intracavernosal injection therapy. Moreover, it activates proerectile signaling pathways (EP2/PKA/CREB) and suppresses the TGF-β/Smad pathway, markedly alleviating cavernosal fibrosis. This work presents a paradigm for noninvasive diabetes mellitus–induced erectile dysfunction therapy.

title: Human hair–bearing skin organoids reveal cell type–specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1
abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. To model this complex environment, we used human hair–bearing skin organoids and combined single-cell spatial transcriptomics with imaging to map viral spread and host responses across skin architecture. Our data suggest delayed progression of the HSV-1 life cycle in epidermal keratinocytes and hair follicle cells compared to the dermis. Infection triggered spatially organized host responses, including induction of IER3 in papillary fibroblasts. In basal keratinocytes, IRF3 was up-regulated in both infected and neighboring uninfected cells, consistent with paracrine activation of antiviral signaling. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type–specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor–α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α–responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α–expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair–bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host–HSV-1 interactions.

title: General prediction of T cell receptor antigen specificity from sequence using AlphaFold 3
abstract: The major histocompatibility complex (MHC):peptide:T cell receptor (TCR) complex is the most diverse trimolecular interface known in nature and a key trigger for adaptive immunity. TCRs are now routinely sequenced at scale; however, decoding their specificity for antigens remains a bottleneck. While in silico approaches have advanced considerably, none enables prediction against “unseen” epitopes, limiting their applicability to a tiny fraction of cases. Here, we show that AlphaFold 3 (AF3) predicts the structures of MHC:peptide:TCR triads with unprecedented accuracy. By applying AF3 to >9000 TCRs mapped to >1000 distinct epitopes restricted by >70 MHC class I/II alleles, we identify features that distinguish cognate triads from controls. The resulting model achieves median areas under the curve of 0.81 to 0.92 on validation triads unseen by AF3 or during feature selection. Our results reveal that generalized prediction of TCR specificity from sequence is possible, with the potential to greatly accelerate the decoding of immune responses.

title: Intrinsic cellular persistent firing sustains hippocampal spatial representations during working memory
abstract: Neurons are the fundamental units of cognitive processing. The prevailing view holds that neurons are input-output units that fire action potentials only upon receiving sufficient synaptic input. Here, we demonstrate that this may not be the sole operational mode of neurons in vivo during cognitive tasks, by showing that hippocampal place cells actively maintain firing and preserve spatial information through molecularly defined intrinsic mechanisms. Using in vitro and in vivo recordings coupled with molecular manipulation in mice, we reveal that hippocampal persistent firing during spatial working memory is supported by individual neurons via TRPC4 ion channels. Despite the general belief that persistent activity maintains working memory content, we demonstrate that persistent firing instead maintains immediate spatial representations, potentially supporting the encoding of spatial information to guide behavior. These findings position individual neurons as active contributors to information retention, extending their traditional role as passive input-output units and potentially broadening our understanding of neural computation.

title: Tunneling spectroscopy of topological insulator Josephson junctions
abstract: In the seminal proposal by Fu and Kane, the superconducting proximity effect is used to realize topological superconductivity in the topological surface state (TSS) of a 3D topological insulator (TI). In a Josephson junction made on the TI surface, the spin-momentum locking of the TSS guarantees the existence of spin nondegenerate, perfectly transmitted Andreev modes. These modes lead to gap closing as a function of the superconducting phase difference φ. Here, we report the observation of highly transmissive Andreev modes in a TI Josephson junction, probed via tunnel contacts and φ controlled by a flux loop. Within our experimental resolution, they could indicate a gap closing and reopening. This phenomenon is observed for a wide range of chemical potentials, supporting its TSS origin. Under an applied magnetic field, highly transmissive modes are observed locally, matching theoretical predictions for Josephson vortices in the TSS. Our results support the fundamental role of spin-momentum locking in the Andreev physics in the TSS.

title: LAMP2A gene therapy mitigates Parkinson’s disease–related pathology in nonhuman primates
abstract: Chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA), regulated by its lysosomal receptor LAMP2A, is a key pathway for αSynuclein (αSyn) clearance and a direct target of αSyn-related neurotoxicity. Rodent studies show that LAMP2A enhancement reverses neurodegeneration, whereas its deficiency accelerates pathology. To test translational relevance, we examined whether increasing LAMP2A expression in nonhuman primates could mitigate α-synucleinopathy induced by injections of Parkinson’s disease patient-derived Lewy body (LB) extract. Increasing LAMP2A expression protected nigral dopaminergic neurons from LB-induced αSyn neurodegeneration, delayed the formation and release of pathology-related αSyn species, and evoked a beneficial effect on motor behavior and on cognitive functions of the primate model. Our findings provide preliminary preclinical evidence supporting CMA enhancement as a therapeutic strategy for αSynucleinopathies.

title: PDS5A and TOP2B cooperate for chromatin recruitment via CTCF
abstract: PDS5A, a cohesin regulatory subunit, and topoisomerase IIB (TOP2B), an enzyme resolving DNA topological problems, interact with CTCF and regulate transcription and genome organization. We ascertained that PDS5A and TOP2B are recruited to CTCF-bound chromatin cooperatively and that catalytically active TOP2B increases PDS5A occupancy genome wide. Notably, the amino-terminal 95 to 116 amino acids of CTCF interacts with PDS5A, giving rise to CTCF-PDS5A-TOP2B interaction in vitro and to PDS5A chromatin enrichment via active TOP2B in vivo. PDS5A-TOP2B function together in moderating the resultant gene expression and genome organization. Loss of CTCF (95 to 116 amino acids) led to dysregulated gene expression and mildly reduced chromatin loops. In gliomas, PDS5A and TOP2B expression levels vary, but correlate, contributing to distinctive gene expression patterns. Inducible PDS5A knockdown led to reduced TOP2B occupancy and altered gene expression. Furthermore, PDS5A mediated sensitivity to TOP2 cancer drugs in glioma cells. This functional interaction between PDS5A and TOP2B at CTCF boundaries expands upon the mechanisms affecting gene regulation through genome organization, with implications for glioma therapeutics.

title: Cryo-EM structure of a protein nanopore reveals lipid acyl chains as integral components
abstract: Nanopore-based technologies are revolutionizing nucleic acid sequencing and molecular sensing, yet the structural basis by which pore-forming proteins interact with lipid membranes remains poorly defined. The mycobacterial porin MspA is a benchmark biological nanopore owing to its exceptional stability and uniquely narrow constriction, but accurate structural information is limited to protein-only models. Here, we present a 2.5-angstrom resolution cryo–electron microscopy structure of the M2 mutant of MspA embedded in a phospholipid nanodisc, providing a high-resolution experimental observation of MspA in a lipid environment. The structure reveals an annular arrangement of extended lipid acyl chains surrounding the MspA oligomer and contacting the transmembrane barrel. Their resolved densities indicate a substantially more ordered annular lipid environment than would be expected from a largely heterogeneous and nonspecific protein-lipid interface. The structure also demonstrates how specific M2 MspA mutations modulate pore polarity, influencing ion selectivity and transport. By determining the membrane-embedded structure of MspA and revealing an ordered arrangement of acyl chains forming extensive hydrophobic interactions with the protein, this study demonstrates the importance of the surrounding lipid environment in the design of protein nanopores.

title: A-site cation–pseudohalide co-design for tin halide perovskite transistors
abstract: Tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free semiconductors for next-generation electronics; however, their implementation is constrained by a fragile crystal framework, facile Sn2+oxidation, and rapid crystallization kinetics. Here, we establish a molecular design principle for non-metallic thiocyanate (SCN−) additives that stabilizes the formamidinium tin iodide (FASnI3) lattice and enables high-performance, stable p-channel thin-film transistors (TFTs). Density functional theory calculations reveal that the Sn–X–Sn bond strength in the lattice and the halide migration barriers can be tuned by the size of the A-site cation and its hydrogen-bonding capability with SCN−and I−. In particular, we find that both the Sn–SCN–Sn bonding interaction and the iodine migration barrier are maximized when guanidinium thiocyanate (GuaSCN) is employed. Consistently, GuaSCN enhances the crystallinity and grain size of tens-of-nanometer-thick FASnI3films, prolongs carrier lifetimes, and suppresses Sn4+formation, without altering the intrinsic bandgap. TFTs incorporating GuaSCN achieve a field-effect mobility above 88 cm2V−1s−1, anIon/offratio exceeding 4 × 109, negligible hysteresis, and superior operational and shelf stability across hundreds of devices.

title: Electric field–controlled spin transport in a topological insulator interfaced with a ferroelectric antiferromagnet
abstract: Topological insulators have been explored extensively for spin-charge interconversion via magnetic interfaces, yet the true response of their spin-charge conversion, particularly in the absence of an external magnetic field, remains to be studied. Here, we report electric field control of spin-charge conversion in the topological insulator Bi2Te3with the antiferromagnetic multiferroic BiFeO3, using a nonlocal spin transport device. A systematic thickness dependence of the spin transport across the interface between Bi2Te3and BiFeO3reveals a signature of topological surface-state–dominated spin transport in the bilayer system. The spin-charge conversion remains robust for thicknesses above 10 nanometers but falls rapidly with reducing thickness and vanishes at 5 nanometers. This is consistent with hybridization-induced emergence of a trivial insulating phase, which is supported by the coherency factor estimated from the magnetoconductance of Bi2Te3. These results establish that spin-momentum–locked surface states dominate interfacial spin transport in the decoupled regime. Beyond presenting efficient spin-charge interconversion at an entirely insulating magnetic interface, this work also highlights sputter-deposited Bi2Te3as a high-quality and scalable platform for integrating quantum materials onto the devices. The nonlocal spin transport approach presented here provides a simple and unprecedented direct evidence of spin-charge conversion and opens an efficient and practical pathway toward designing energy-efficient spin-based devices.

title: Rashba-induced intersubband interference in high-harmonic generation
abstract: High-harmonic spectroscopy is exquisitely sensitive to the electronic structure and dynamics of quantum materials, yet quantum interference between spin-orbit-split bands has remained experimentally elusive. We observe this interference between Rashba-split bands in bismuth tellurium iodide (BiTeI) driven by strong mid-infrared laser fields. The sixth harmonic exhibits intensity-scaling kinks and an M-shaped ellipticity dependence. Theoretical simulations attribute these features to spin-orbit–mediated multichannel quantum interference, which arises from Landau-Zener-Stückelberg–type intersubband tunneling between Rashba-split bands. The suppression of harmonic yield under linearly polarized pulses arises from destructive interference among electron-hole recombination pathways, whereas increasing ellipticity modifies their relative phase and induces a distinct spectral redshift. These results establish high-harmonic spectroscopy as a probe of spin-textured band dynamics and ultrafast spin-polarized currents.

title: Mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming by a glutamine antagonist radioenhancer conjugate drives pyroptosis and antitumor immunity
abstract: Aberrant glutamine metabolism undermines the efficacy of cancer radiotherapy (RT) by promoting DNA repair, increasing oxygen consumption, and imposing metabolic stress that compromises the viability and function of cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs). Here, we report a mitochondria-enriched, metabolism-regulating monolayered metal-organic framework (MOF) nanoplatform, Hf-Ir/DON, constructed by incorporating the glutamine antagonist 6-diazo-5-oxo-l-norleucine (DON) into a radiosensitizing hafnium-iridium (Hf-Ir) MOF to inhibit glutaminolysis. This design markedly sensitizes tumor cells to RT and, upon x-ray irradiation, enables mitochondria-targeted RT-radiodynamic therapy with substantially enhanced reactive oxygen species accumulation. The resulting oxidative stress induces extensive DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and immunogenic tumor cell pyroptosis. Concurrently, Hf-Ir/DON alleviates metabolic constraints on activated T cells, preserving CTL viability while sustaining effector and memory functions. In a murine colon cancer model, low-dose RT combined with Hf-Ir/DON achieved >95% tumor growth inhibition. Further combination with anti–PD-L1 therapy induced regression of bilateral triple-negative breast tumors and prevented lung metastasis. These results establish a radiometabolic MOF nanoplatform that potentiates RT while promoting durable antitumor immunity.

title: A skin-like, all-in-one hydrogel engineered via a supramolecular entangled network reinforced with hydrogen-bond–associated nanodomains
abstract: Hydrogels hold substantial promise for artificial skin in bionic robotics and biomedical devices. However, few hydrogels have a combination of properties comparable to natural human skin. Here, we report a skin-like, all-in-one hydrogel based on a supramolecular entangled network reinforced with hydrogen-bond–associated nanodomains. Within this architecture, hydrogen-bond–associated self-assembled nanodomains, polymer-chain entanglement, dynamic electrostatic interactions, and reversible metal-ligand coordination operate cooperatively to endow the network with mechanical robustness and dynamic adaptability. Consequently, the hydrogel reconciles the intrinsic trade-offs among mechanical properties, multiple functions, and multimodal perception. Its integrated performance compares favorably with that of other advanced hydrogels and even biological skin. To demonstrate its potential applications, we constructed an artificial skin using our hydrogel, which facilitates interaction with the surrounding environment, including monitoring respiration, detecting motion, and manipulating robotic grippers. These results pave the way for versatile hydrogels that replicate the unparalleled combinatory properties of natural skin more precisely for diverse intelligent applications.

title: Alleviating the stability-energy density dilemma via electron-donor-mediated orbital symmetry regulation in sodium phosphate cathodes
abstract: Manganese-based sodium super ionic conductor-type cathode materials, leveraging the multielectron redox activity of manganese, represent a promising pathway toward high-energy-density sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, the unavoidable generation of Mn3+(3d4) species during charge-discharge processes, characterized by asymmetric egorbital occupancy, triggers octahedral symmetry breaking. This inherent electronic structural instability creates a fundamental contradiction between achieving high energy density and ensuring long cycle life that remains inherently difficult to reconcile. Here, we report an electron-donor–mediated (EDM) mechanism that suppresses Mn3+-induced octahedral distortion while preserving high-spin functionality. As electron-donating Fe3+and V3+are incorporated, Mn3+3d electrons undergo partial delocalization. This electronic redistribution promotes orbital interactions between neighboring transition metal sites through the transition metal-oxygen framework, driving the egorbitals toward a more symmetric occupation and suppressing octahedral distortion. The EDM-modified cathode demonstrates a high energy density of 492.06 Wh kg−1. It delivers 178.8 mAh g−1at 0.1 C and retains 80.2% of its capacity over 2000 cycles at 10 C, paving a novel pathway toward next-generation high-performance SIBs cathode materials.

authors: Samir Lalani;Samuel Haddox;Kendall Bromley;Shafaque Zahra;Marina Wang;Mason Ingram;Sehajroop Gadh;Shriya Gunalan;Sulun Ke;Qiong Wang;Fujun Qin;Eric Hendrickson;Anja Bielinsky;Hui Li
title: Integrative discovery and functional dependency mapping uncover essential chimeric RNAs in the active transcriptome
abstract: Chimeric RNAs are a class of molecules defined as RNA transcripts containing genetic information for multiple genes. While their expression patterns across tissue types and disease states have been well documented, the biological function of these transcripts remains poorly understood. In this study, we developed an integrative prediction pipeline to establish an atlas of 569,640 chimeric RNAs across 1019 cancer cell lines. Leveraging this resource, we performed a systematic functional dependency screen by integrating our predictions with perturbation datasets from The Cancer Dependency Map project. This approach moves beyond prediction to identifying high-confidence functional chimeric RNAs essential for cellular processes, including a subset of recurrent chimeric transcripts generated by cis-splicing of adjacent genes. We demonstrate that depletion of selected candidate chimeras disrupts cell cycle progression and cellular fitness and that these transcripts are frequently dysregulated in primary breast tumors. Together, these results demonstrate that chimeric RNAs constitute a previously underappreciated layer of gene expression, expanding the functional genome beyond conventional genetics.

title: Competing charge and spin instabilities and giant magnetoelastic coupling in CrSb
abstract: Electronic, magnetic, and lattice degrees of freedom are often strongly intertwined in quantum materials, giving rise to competing ordered states and emergent collective phenomena. Understanding how these interactions evolve across symmetry-breaking transitions is essential for identifying new mechanisms of electronic ordering. Here, we show that the antiferromagnet chromium antimonide provides an ideal platform to investigate this interplay and uncover short-range charge-order fluctuations at theMpoint of the Brillouin zone,q* =(120), persisting well above the Néel temperature,TN. These fluctuations collapse upon entering the magnetically ordered phase, revealing a direct competition between charge and spin order parameters. AtTN, the phonon dispersion atq* develops a pronounced Kohn-like anomaly, signaling strong electron-phonon coupling in the vicinity of the magnetic transition. BelowTN, exchange striction markedly renormalizes the associated soft phonon mode by ∼6 milli–electron volts, corresponding to the largest spin-phonon coupling reported to date. First-principles calculations show that the relevant phonon branch is unstable at the harmonic level only in the absence of magnetic order, highlighting the remarkable sensitivity of the lattice to magnetic symmetry breaking. The suppression of charge correlations upon magnetic ordering, together with the abrupt reconstruction of the phonon spectrum atTN, demonstrates an exceptional coupling between charge, spin, and lattice degrees of freedom in chromium antimonide. With its chemically simple structure and symmetry-protected altermagnetic state, chromium antimonide emerges as a model system for exploring giant spin-phonon coupling, competing electronic instabilities, and emergent broken symmetries in altermagnetic materials.

title: Extracellular vesicle-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74–NF-κB repairs diabetic neuropathy
abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) affects up to half of people with diabetes and lacks disease-modifying therapy. Here, we profiled MSC-EV biodistribution and multiomic programs across diabetic models, with key nerve repair established in db/db mice and corroborated in high-fat diet/streptozotocin- and methionine-choline–deficient mice. Systemically administered EVs predominantly accumulated in the liver and improved peripheral nerve structure and function, with benefits supported by glycemia-controlled or glycemia-adjusted analyses rather than being fully explained by systemic glycemic changes. EV treatment was associated with reduced circulating injury markers, attenuated spinal inflammatory responses, and improved endothelial junction integrity. Mechanistically, EV-encapsulated miR-24-3p repressed hepatic CD74, coinciding with reduced MHC II/NF-κB activity in macrophages. Hepatic CD74 overexpression promoted systemic inflammation and peripheral nerve injury, whereas pharmacologic NF-κB inhibition recapitulated EV-associated benefits. Together, these data define a liver-to-nerve causal axis and support EV-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74–NF-κB signaling as a cross-organ strategy for DPN repair.

title: The true scale of global wildlife trade is obscured by data gaps
abstract: Overexploitation of wildlife is one of the greatest global drivers of biodiversity loss. Yet, despite this well-established risk, data on extraction and trade are both incomplete and highly fragmented. The IPBES Global analysis estimated 50,000 species to be in trade, yet our review of wildlife trade monitoring programs found at least double that, at 107,356 species in use and trade globally. This included up to 47,685 animal species, covering 42% of all described vertebrate species. Most countries lack any systematic data on trade for species not listed in Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), with the exception of the US-specific dataset Law Enforcement Management Information System, which frequently had higher diversity of species in trade than global databases. This highlights the importance of national monitoring efforts and the need for standardized collation of wildlife trade data beyond CITES-listed species. Without these changes, global indicators on trade meant to guide sustainability and conservation will continue to focus on less than 2% of traded species.

title: ANME-2a perform methane oxidation in brackish coastal sediments via multiple pathways
abstract: Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas. Typically, a large fraction of methane formed in coastal sediments is removed via anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM). Here, we demonstrate the potential for a range of AOM pathways in brackish coastal sediments by ANME-2a archaea. At our study site, geochemical profiles indicate that AOM is primarily restricted to a shallow, metal oxide–rich sulfate-methane transition zone (SMTZ). ANME-2a were the sole methanotrophs detected, and metatranscriptomics showed the highest expression levels of the ANME-2a genes in the SMTZ. AOM activity was observed in sediment incubations with various electron acceptors, including sulfate, metal oxides, and the organic matter analog graphene oxide. Highest potential rates were observed in sediments from below the SMTZ, pointing toward fast stimulation of the deeper methanotrophic community when alleviating the electron acceptor limitation. The variety of AOM pathways and persistence of methanotrophs below the SMTZ likely contribute to the resilience of the microbial methane filter in brackish coastal sediments.

title: Crystalline three-dimensional membranes enable chromatography-free purification of natural products
abstract: Chromatographic purification of natural products is solvent intensive and energy-demanding and remains a major bottleneck in the sustainable production of pharmaceutical compounds. Here, we show that crystalline three-dimensional membranes enable chromatography-free purification of complex natural product mixtures by organic solvent nanofiltration. The rigid, nanomechanically robust channels of the membrane sustain continuous 6-day operation with commercialTaxuscrude extracts, achieving ∼96% retention and fourfold enrichment of paclitaxel while allowing valuable precursors to permeate. The membranes exhibit high solvent permeance with negligible swelling, enabling stable molecular sieving in methanol across extended operation. Scalable fabrication via nanosphere-assembled interfacial polymerization produces continuous crystalline membranes over large areas. Life cycle assessment reveals nearly an order-of-magnitude reduction in carbon emissions compared with liquid chromatography. These results demonstrate a membrane platform that can replace chromatographic steps in natural product drug purification, offering a sustainable route for active pharmaceutical ingredient production.

title: Elevated CO2 mitigated warming-enhanced carbon loss from northern peatland
abstract: Peatlands store one-third of the global soil carbon (C) on only ∼3% of Earth’s land surface but risk becoming C sources to accelerate climate change due to warming-induced C loss. Elevated CO2(eCO2) may mitigate this loss by boosting plant C uptake. However, how eCO2and climate warming interact to influence peatland C dynamics remains unclear. Here, we investigated peatland C fate at five warming levels (+0°, +2.25°, +4.5°, +6.75°, and + 9°C), each under ambient CO2(aCO2) and eCO2(+500 parts per million), by model-guided synthesis of 18 measured variables for each of the 10 treatments from an experiment. Our results showed that the peatland C loss increased with warming at a rate of 62.6 g C m−2year−1°C−1, reaching 476.5 ± 104.7 g C m−2year−1at +9°C under aCO2, primarily because of increasedSphagnummortality and accelerated decomposition. eCO2reduced the loss rate to 17.3 g C m−2year−1°C−1, nearly halving the C loss at +9°C (269.4 ± 80.5 g C m−2year−1), mainly due to enhanced tree and shrub growth. Methane emissions increased with warming, similarly under aCO2and eCO2. Our findings suggest that northern peatlands likely become major C sources under climate warming, although rising atmospheric CO2concentration may partially slow down the C loss. Climate-driven shifts in plant community structure, rather than peat decomposition alone, play a critical role in regulating peatland C fate and may threaten the stability of peatland ecosystem functions and services in the future.

title: Oxygen-dependent constraint of glycolysis through the mitochondrial electron transport chain
abstract: Hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs) are constitutively active in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) cells. Here, we investigated whether these cells could still respond to hypoxia independently of canonical HIF activation. We found that hypoxia provokes a NADH reductive stress that attenuates lactate release when the supply of extracellular pyruvate becomes limited, a response that was restored by the ectopic expression of the cytosolic and mitochondria-targeted NADH oxidase (LbNOX). Suppression of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (mtETC) alone is sufficient to attenuate glycolytic flux when extracellular pyruvate is limited, a situation consistent with metabolomic data from human ccRCCs. Furthermore, this response can be mimicked by pharmacological or genetic inhibition of mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) activity and restored by the mitochondrial-targeted alternative oxidase (AOX). Therefore, our data suggest that cells can respond to low oxygen tension through a mitochondrial-dependent elevation of NADH/NAD+, resulting in the suppression of glycolysis when pyruvate availability is compromised.

authors: Yang Qu;Yihan Xu;Jingchao Bai;Yuhan Zhang;Ning Ji;Xinxin Li;Hui Li
title: GPR183 senses 7α,25-OHC to drive Treg differentiation and tumor immune evasion via AXL-JAK2-STAT5 signaling
abstract: Regulatory T cell (Treg) accumulation within the tumor microenvironment is a major contributor to immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance. However, the metabolic signals orchestrating Treglineage commitment remain poorly defined. We identify that the oxysterol 7α,25-dihydroxycholesterol (7α,25-OHC), produced by Vimentin+stromal cells, acts through GPR183 to promote Tregdifferentiation and suppressive identity. In patients with gastric cancer (GC), GPR183+Treginfiltration correlates with advanced disease and poor survival. In syngeneic tumor models, conditional GPR183 deletion, specifically in CD4+T cells or Tregcells, demonstrates its cell-intrinsic requirement for high-cholesterol-diet–induced Tregexpansion and tumor growth, thereby abrogating immune evasion and restoring CD8+T cell effector function. Mechanistically, 7α,25-OHC–GPR183 signaling activates the AXL-JAK2-STAT5 pathway to reinforce Foxp3 expression. Last, GPR183 antagonism modestly enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy in a model-dependent manner and prevents therapy-induced Tregexpansion. These findings identify the 7α,25-OHC–GPR183–AXL axis as a potential metabolic checkpoint linking cholesterol metabolism to immune suppression, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy to enhance antitumor immunity.

title: The Fireside Database: Large-scale evidence from 25,419 psychedelic support interactions
abstract: Most psychedelic experiences occur outside clinical settings, yet as policy frameworks rapidly expand to accommodate nonclinical use, no systematic data exist on who seeks psychedelic support, under what circumstances, or what makes that support effective. We present the Fireside Database, a US-based dataset comprising 25,419 peer support interactions conducted by 220 trained volunteers at Fireside Project’s Psychedelic Support Line between April 2021 and February 2026. The released resource integrates structured interaction logs with volunteer-coded metadata and 2777 caller satisfaction surveys across five outcome dimensions. Psilocybin was the most commonly reported substance (59.9% of coded interactions), while cannabis produced the highest distress rate (47.2%). The nested data structure—with 50 supporters each completing ≥10 surveyed interactions—supports multilevel modeling of individual supporter effects on caller outcomes. This resource enables research in psychedelic epidemiology, evidence-based training design, and the investigation of what makes psychedelic psychological support effective.

title: Metazoan diversification characterized by elevated rates of evolution during the middle Ediacaran to earliest Cambrian
abstract: To test causal hypotheses for the emergence of animal body plans, we analyze rates of molecular and phenotypic evolution across Opisthokonta, focusing on divergences within the Tonian-Ordovician interval. Both molecular and phenotypic rates increase through the Ediacaran, peaking in an Ediacaran and earliest Cambrian interval before declining thereafter. Partitioning phenotypic characters into categories relating to development, feeding, fossilization potential, locomotion, and nervous systems reveals distinct temporal patterns, with developmental traits contributing disproportionately to elevated rates in the metazoan stem lineage. Rate patterns show a temporal lag between the ecological changes integral to hypotheses of developmental evolution and the Cambrian agronomic, substrate, and information revolutions and earlier peaks in the evolution of the associated phenotypic characters. These patterns are largely independent of the timescale used. Overall, our results indicate that the primary phase of elevated evolutionary novelty occurred during the Ediacaran and culminated in the late Ediacaran-earliest Cambrian, providing the foundation for later ecological and taxonomic innovation.

title: A dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle delivery system for precision phage therapy against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria
abstract: The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria, demands innovative therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle-chimeric phage (AbLCP) system engineered to combat multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria. Our design integrates a genetically modified M13 phage displaying anti–lipopolysaccharide (LPS) antibodies with polymyxin B conjugation, which is further encapsulated within anti-LPS antibody–functionalized lipid nanoparticles. This system overcomes the fundamental limitations of conventional phage therapy, enabling efficient cellular internalization, endosomal escape, and potent intracellular bactericidal activity. In murine models ofPseudomonas aeruginosainfection, AbLCP achieved superior bacterial clearance and up to 103-fold reduction in bacterial burden at a 103-fold lower effective dose than free polymyxin B, with 67-fold selective accumulation at infection sites, and attenuated systemic inflammation and preservation of gut microbiota. Mechanistically, AbLCP neutralized LPS to suppress inflammation and induced a lethal bacterial stress response. This work establishes a transformative nanophage platform that merges synthetic biology with nanomedicine, offering a promising strategy against MDR bacterial infections.

title: Monolithic and scalable capacitive electrodes leveraging parasitic capacitance for full-body pressure mapping
abstract: Scaling capacitive pressure sensor arrays to large areas remains challenging due to electrode alignment errors, fabrication complexity, and limited dynamic range inherent in conventional parallel-plate architectures. Here, we present a scalable capacitive pressure sensor array based on a monolithic electrode architecture, where transmitter and receiver electrodes are co-integrated into a single substrate. A deformable dielectric and a floating ground (GND) layer are positioned above, eliminating alignment errors and reducing the layer-stacking process by 20%. The parasitic capacitance between the electrodes and GND layer is intentionally incorporated into the sensing mechanism, enabling stable pressure detection with effective electromagnetic interference shielding. The resulting 2911-cell array (1.7 m by 1.0 m) achieves 30 Hz full-body pressure mapping with high linearity (R2= 0.994). Demonstrations in sleep posture classification, pressure injury prevention, and exercise monitoring validate the platform’s versatility for healthcare and human-machine interfaces.

title: Fluid-driven robotic micromanipulation for assembloid fabrication
abstract: The assembly of cellular spheroids into spatially organized assembloids represents a transformative paradigm for modeling complex biological systems. However, the lack of standardized fabrication strategies fundamentally limits the precision and reproducibility of these models, hindering their widespread application. Here, we present a robotic micromanipulation platform—Fluid-Driven Tweezer with Visual Servo Control (FDT-VSC). By integrating multidimensional visual perception with microfluidic control, our system enables the gentle and programmable assembly of diverse cellular spheroids. Leveraging this platform, we achieve the bottom-up construction of structurally defined, heterogeneous multicellular tissues, and the programmed orchestration of multilineage models that recapitulate the complex microenvironments of early organogenesis. Crucially, the system improves consistency during the scalable fabrication of tumor-stroma assembloids, supporting reliable drug screening. These results demonstrate that FDT-VSC advances assembloid-based applications across modular tissue engineering, developmental biology, and drug discovery.

authors: Cosimo E. Carniel;Jonathan D. Wille;Lukas Brunner;Diana Francis;Erich M. Fischer
title: Coarse climate model grids underestimate coastal humid-heat extremes
abstract: Humid-heat extremes reach intensities close to the limit of human survivability around the Arabian Peninsula. Here, we analyze fully coupled kilometer-scale Icosahedral Nonhydrostatic (ICON) and Integrated Forecasting System–FinitevolumE Sea ice-Ocean Model (IFS-FESOM) simulations from the nextGEMS project, with original resolutions of around 9 kilometers, and compare them with station observations, ERA5, and CMIP6 projections. IFS-FESOM reproduces well the observed upper-tail wet-bulb temperature (TW) and lies near the high end of the CMIP6 distribution over coastal regions, while ICON simulates weaker extremes. Spatial smoothing suppresses localized coastal maxima, reducing daily-maximum TW extremes by up to 8°C and lowering exceedance frequencies across multiple thresholds. Native resolution fields also show stronger mid-century increases in exposure under SSP3-7.0 than their coarse-gridded counterparts. These results suggest that conventional coarse resolution projections may underestimate localized coastal humid-heat risk, although the magnitude of this effect remains model dependent.

title: Photosynthetic chimeric stem cells function as mitochondrial batteries
abstract: Therapies built on mitochondrial transfer hold promise for repairing dysfunctional, energy-deficient cells. Still, mesenchymal stem cells used as mitochondrial donors are limited by poor engraftment, risk of aberrant differentiation, and low transfer efficiency. Herein, we constructed photosynthesis-empowered cross-kingdom chimeric stem cells (PCSs; “mitochondrial battery”) by introducing plant-derived thylakoid-based artificial nuclei plusFGF21-encoding messenger RNA (mRNA) into enucleated bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Photosynthetic activity enhances mitochondrial transfer to restore metabolism in damaged cells and elevates anabolism to increase FGF21 production. Sustained FGF21 release promotes mitochondrial biogenesis and sustains long-term cellular energy homeostasis. Mouse and porcine wound healing models demonstrate that PCSs recharge cellular energy to accelerate wound repair. This light-activated cellular photosynthetic platform supports modular mRNA programmability, shows no engraftment or aberrant differentiation, and allows repeated administration for diverse therapeutic applications.

authors: Ga-eun Go;Seungju Han;Minjae Kang;Sangoh Choi;Soo-eun Lee;Uidon Jeong;Sang-Hee Lee;Ki-Nam Gu;Hanji Kim;Bo Kyoung Hwang;Yunkwan Kim;Euitaek Jeong;Nae-Gyu Kang;Doory Kim
title: Super-resolution mapping of nuclear stress signaling by probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles in UV-induced skin photodamage
abstract: Ultraviolet (UV)-induced photodamage drives oxidative stress, DNA damage, and chronic inflammation, leading to progressive cellular ultrastructure and skin function degeneration. Despite the potential of probiotics as anti-photodamage agents, their nanoscale action mechanism remains unexplored. Here, we utilize super-resolution fluorescence microscopy to investigate the cellular and molecular basis ofLactobacillus plantarum-derived extracellular vesicles (L. plantarumEVs) in mitigating photodamage. We showed that UV irradiation triggered extensive organellar remodeling along with elevated reactive oxygen species production, DNA damage signaling, and inflammatory activation. Remarkably, pre- and posttreatment withL. plantarumEVs preserved organelle integrity and restored native nanoscale architecture. Additionally, EV treatment delayed UV-induced PARP-1 activation and nuclear condensate clustering, while suppressing NF-κB translocation and downstream inflammatory cytokine expression. These findings establish probiotic-derived EVs as modulators of stress-responsive signaling and structural homeostasis during UV-induced photodamage. By providing a super-resolution mechanistic framework for understanding probiotic EV-mediated modulation of cellular photodamage responses, this study provides a basis for future investigation of EV-based strategies for skin protection.

authors: Shlomit Sharoni;Keisuke Inomura;Stephanie Dutkiewicz;Oliver Jahn;Gregory L. Britten;Michael J. Follows
title: C:H:N:O:P stoichiometry and oxygen demand of marine organic matter are driven by phytoplankton ecophysiology
abstract: Although the hydrogen and oxygen content of marine phytoplankton plays a critical role in determining oceanic O2consumption rates, shaping habitat for anaerobic metabolism, they are often assumed to be constant in biogeochemical studies, resulting in biased estimates of respiration rates. Here, by simulating phytoplankton allocation in a general circulation model, we predict latitudinal variations in phytoplankton C:H:N:O:P composition and corresponding O2demand. These patterns are driven by physiological adaptation to environmental conditions and are consistent with observations. Subtropical phytoplankton have more C─O bonds and lower O2demand, as they contain more carbohydrates than higher-latitude populations. We test the sensitivity of O2inventory and regenerated C via the biological pump (Csoft) to plausible bounds of cellular allocation and find that the global O2inventory and Csoftdecrease by ∼11 and 14%, respectively, when a cell shifts from carbohydrate-rich to protein-rich biomass. Our findings demonstrate that biochemical remodeling of phytoplankton composition mediates large-scale patterns and oceanic budgets of O2and C.

authors: John Soukar;Kayli Jones;Natalie M. Garza;Valeria Duran Salas;Shounak Roy;Vishal M. Gohil;Akhilesh K. Gaharwar
title: Augmenting intercellular mitochondrial transfer for tissue repair and rejuvenation
abstract: Cells exhibit innate reparative communication, enabling the exchange of bioactive molecules and, in some cases, entire organelles. Harnessing this endogenous process of intercellular organelle transfer represents an emerging therapeutic paradigm for restoring cellular function in diseases driven by organelle dysfunction. Mitochondrial transfer has gained prominence for its ability to restore bioenergetic capacity, mitigate oxidative stress, and rescue metabolic function in cells with impaired mitochondrial activity. Given that genetic or acquired defects in mitochondrial function are associated with diverse pathologies, including neurodegeneration, cardiovascular diseases, metabolic disorders, skeletal muscle defects, immune dysregulation, and age-associated decline, mitochondrial transfer offers broad therapeutic potential. Mitochondrial transfer seeks to deliver functional mitochondria to injured cells to reestablish metabolic competence. However, insufficient organelle trafficking and limited control over transfer dynamics remain critical barriers to clinical translation. Recent biotechnological developments aimed at enhancing donor-recipient connectivity, increasing mitochondrial availability, and modulating transfer machinery have begun to address some of these key challenges. This review highlights recent advances in mitochondrial transfer bioengineering, emerging therapeutic applications, and key challenges that must be resolved to enable clinical deployment.
